articles.title: Aaron Philo, Florida beat No. 11 Kentucky to likely dash Wildcats' CFP hopes
articles.summary: The quarterback, weeks after getting benched, put up more than 100 rushing yards on the way to the Gators' 21-14 win.
articles.body:
The College Football Playoff continues to get shaken up, as Florida defeated No. 11 Kentucky 21-14 behind a strong second half.

The Gators' win came off a big night from quarterback Aaron Philo on the ground as he rushed for 102 yards and a touchdown. But for the Wildcats, the surprise home loss all but dashes their chances at the CFP.

The second-half collapse for Kentucky gives the Wildcats (7-3) their second straight loss after getting rolled by Tennessee last weekend. With three losses on the season, Kentucky will slip out of playoff position and will face a tough path to fight their way back in with two games to go.

Florida's only first-half points came in unusual fashion: The team recorded a safety after an offensive holding penalty against Kentucky was called in the end zone. That cut the Wildcats' lead to 7-2 at halftime.

Then, just two plays into the second half, Florida's Jayden Woods sacked Kentucky quarterback Kenny Minchey, forcing a fumble that the Gators recovered. The play gave Florida excellent field position, which they converted into a go-ahead 1-yard touchdown from Jadan Baugh. Philo then secured the 2-point conversion to give the Gators 10-7 lead.

The Wildcats recovered with a touchdown on the next drive to take a 14-10 lead, which Florida later cut to 14-13. But after a Kentucky three-and-out, the Gators followed up with an epic 14-play, 67-yard drive that ended with another touchdown — and another 2-point conversion — to go up 21-14 in the fourth quarter.

Defensive pressure led each team to turn it over on downs on back-to-back drives, with the Gators falling short after a pivotal fourth-down try that would have effectively ended the game. But on fourth-and-2, Baugh came up inches short of a first down, giving Kentucky one last shot.

But the Gators' defense clamped down on the Wildcats, forcing four straight incomplete passes from Minchey to get the ball back and seal the win.

Philo finished the game with 119 passing yards, but his more impressive contribution came on the ground: The quarterback piled up his yardage on 15 attempts, leading the team in rushing.

Philo's big night came just two weeks after he was benched and replaced by Tramell Jones Jr. after throwing two interceptions. Florida, which moves to 6-4, is now bowl-bound after weeks of offensive limbo.

articles.title: Louisville's 16-14 win over North Carolina ends in big brawl
articles.summary: The Cardinals won 16-14.
articles.body:
The Louisville Cardinals went into Chapel Hill and beat North Carolina 16-14.

Tension and frustration from the game finally boiled over right after the Cardinals' quarterback, Lincoln Kienholz, knelt the ball for the final time, ran out the clock, and sealed the win.

It started with a shoving match between linemen and looked like a minor scuffle as the teams parted. But that wasn't the case; a widespread altercation broke out.

A large group of players shoved each other as they moved down the field, with some going to the ground. Other shoving matches broke out elsewhere on the field, and it only got more chaotic as the benches emptied and staff and players got more involved.

Flags came out on the play, but the game was over. After a few minutes of excitement, the sides finally parted, and the normal postgame routine began.

Louisville took an early lead with a first-quarter field goal, but North Carolina responded with a touchdown. By halftime, the Cardinals were leading 13-7. The second half didn't bring too much excitement until the final play. Louisville added a field goal, and North Carolina scored a touchdown with 3:43 left to trail by two.

The Cardinals then punted, giving the Tar Heels a chance. Backup quarterback Travis Burgess — playing for an injured Billy Edwards Jr. — threw an interception, leading to two kneel-downs by Louisville.

North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick had a chance to secure bowl eligibility, but the loss drops the Tar Heels to 5-5. UNC will go on the road to face Virginia next week, before ending the regular season with NC State.

Louisville has won five straight games and is now 7-3 (6-2 ACC). The Cardinals have Pittsburgh next week and end the year with a home game against No. 11 Kentucky. Louisville is currently third in the ACC, and a win against the Panthers next week, along with Wake Forest losing to both Georgia Tech and Duke, would put the Cardinals in the mix for the ACC championship game.

articles.title: 2026 College Football Playoff Bubble Watch After Week 11
articles.summary: We know that more chaos is coming. That part is a given.
articles.body:
We know that more chaos is coming. That part is a given.

A season that has produced an avalanche of upsets, one after the next, isn't done. Where they'll come from and what it means in the grand scheme of our postseason remains unknown, but things will look much different a few weeks from now.

Outside of Georgia, very little in college football is assumed. The Bulldogs are a definitive favorite to win the national championship. The rest seems very much in flux.

What is clear, however, is that the bubble will be hotly contested. Teams with two and three losses will be stacked up against one another and the euphoria and disappointment for programs will be palpable.

As the season winds down, here's a look at the sport's most fascinating bubble teams, where the resumes sit after Week 11 and what's ahead.

Just how good has Wake Forest been of late? Well, in the last four games, the Demon Deacons have outscored their opponents 218-21.

Granted, those four teams included Cal, Virginia, Merrimack and SMU, but the performance has been noteworthy regardless. The team's one loss this year came earlier in the season against Miami, and the game was close enough.

The team is balanced, has a tremendous quarterback in Gio Lopez and has a favorable schedule remaining. Wake Forest plays Georgia Tech and Duke to close out the year.

With two more wins, there might not be all that much debate to be had. In fact, if Wake Forest were to make it to that game and avenge its loss against Miami, it would be guaranteed a spot.

As we weave our way toward teams with two and even three losses, however, we must first assess this team's case. The strength of schedule is dearly lacking, although it probably won't matter.

Well, unless Wake drops one of the next two games. Then the case is over.

The fact that we're using "Oregon" and "bubble" in the same sentence speaks volumes.

Given how bad the season went for the Ducks for a good chunk of the year, the recovery that has taken place, through backup quarterbacks and coordinator changes, is just as unlikely.

Yes, Dante Moore is out for the year. Yes, the team we thought we were getting is nowhere to be found. But Oregon is, at the very least, in the mix.

That's the good news. The bad news is the Big Ten hasn't exactly dazzled this year, and wins over Ohio State, USC and Michigan, which it beat handedly on Saturday, aren't nearly what we thought they'd be. And that ugly, double-digit loss to Illinois is still on the resume.

That loss could very well define the Ducks' playoff faith, especially with extremely winnable games against Michigan State and Washington remaining.

Again, the fact that we're having this conversation is astonishing. But for the Ducks to truly leapfrog other hopeful teams, especially those in the SEC, a lot of help is needed.

BYU's dominating win over Baylor on Saturday was needed. In fact, like most bubble teams, optics the rest of the way are going to be vital.

We could very well be heading toward a familiar situation. The state of the Big 12, and whether the Cougars can play (and win) the conference, could also play a factor. There's a world where BYU plays its way squarely into the tournament.

There's also a good chance we're left comparing resumes, and BYU's is a mixed bag.

Wins over Arizona and, of course, Notre Dame are really nice wins. The loss to UCF will be the one that stings weeks from now.

Games against Kansas and Cincinnati are left, and BYU should be a sizable favorite in both matchups.

That win over Notre Dame should age well. If it does, BYU could very well find its way in.

Let's be clear, Kirk Ferentz's team is probably in need of a little help. That part should go without saying.

But Iowa has continued to win football games, and a dominating win over Purdue on Saturday, while not a huge resume boost, put the Hawkeyes one step closer.

The resume is not pristine, but it's not awful, either. Solid wins over Iowa State, Wisconsin, Washington and Northwestern will help. That ugly loss against Minnesota, however, will not.

The loss against Ohio State? That happens. The Buckeyes were at full strength, and the team was much different than it was not. Still, Ohio State's regression is less than ideal.

First things first, Iowa must win at Illinois and beat Nebraska at home. Neither game is a given, although the Hawkeyes should be favored in both games. If that happens, and the SEC continues to beat itself up, much like it did throughout Week 11, look out.

Iowa's bubble journey is very much alive.

Ohio State has not looked like a College Football Playoff team in some time. Back-to-back losses to USC and Oregon just a few short weeks ago put this team beyond the bubble. In fact, many are questioning whether Ryan Day is the one to lead this team moving forward.

But Ohio State's resume has a few things working for it. For starters, this team played Texas, a legitimate out-of-conference opponent. This particular selection committee seems partial to strength of schedule, and the Buckeyes have that.

The biggest variable, however, is quarterback Julian Sayin. With the QB, Ohio State is a different team. If Sayin is available for the postseason, the committee has a unique situation to evaluate.

First, Ohio State must win at Nebraska, which is no easy feat. It'll have to beat Michigan after that, which seems more than feasible.

Regardless of what the committee thinks about Sayin, Ohio State needs an abundance of help.

articles.title: Indian football's woes continue as Khalid Jamil's men suffer another defeat to New Zealand
articles.summary: India endured another defeat against New Zealand, going down 0-3 in the second international friendly at One New Zealand Stadium in Christchurch on Sunday.
articles.body: India endured another defeat against New Zealand, going down 0-3 in the second international friendly at One New Zealand Stadium in Christchurch on Sunday. After suffering a 0-5 loss in the opening encounter, the Blue Tigers showed some defensive improvement after the break but continued to struggle in attack.New Zealand took control early, putting the Indian defence under sustained pressure through crosses and set-pieces. Their persistence paid off in the 22nd minute when Finn Surman headed home from a corner delivered by McCowatt. The effort took a deflection off Akash Mishra before finding the net, giving the hosts a deserved lead.India struggled to respond, finding it difficult to retain possession and build meaningful attacking moves. The hosts continued to dictate proceedings and doubled their advantage in the 40th minute. McGarry collected the ball following a short corner and unleashed a first-time left-footed strike from the edge of the box, finding the bottom-left corner.The damage was compounded just before half-time. In the 44th minute, Garbett released Randall into the penalty area, and the latter squared the ball for Chris Wood to finish into an unguarded goal, sending New Zealand into the break with a commanding three-goal cushion.Defensive improvement after the breakIndia looked somewhat more organised in the second half, with goalkeeper Hrithik Tiwari, who came on as a substitute, producing an important save to deny McCowatt in the 55th minute. The visitors enjoyed longer spells of possession but struggled to convert them into clear-cut opportunities.Bijoy Varghese also impressed with a crucial goal-line clearance in the 85th minute to prevent Michael Rufer from adding another goal. Tiwari's intervention and Varghese's defensive effort helped India avoid further damage.Attacking struggles remain a concernIndia managed a few attacking moves in the second half. Liston's cross resulted in a corner, while Mehtab Singh tested New Zealand goalkeeper Alex Paulsen, who made a comfortable save. However, Liston later missed an opportunity with a wayward effort in the 80th minute.Despite showing greater defensive resolve after the interval, India failed to find a breakthrough and finished the match without seriously troubling the hosts.The defeat leaves head coach Khalid Jamil with plenty to address, particularly India's lack of attacking penetration, as the team continues its search for improvement against stronger international opposition.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Los caminos que unen Albacete y Vigo
articles.standfirst: Historias compartidas y tres puntos clave para la permanencia, el lunes en el Belmonte
articles.summary: Historias compartidas y tres puntos clave para la permanencia, el lunes en el Belmonte
articles.body: El Albacete cierra el lunes la 14ª jornada en un duelo inédito en la categoría de plata. Los únicos precedentes oficiales se remontan a la temporada 2011-12, cuando el Alba y el filial celeste compartieron grupo en la extinta Segunda B. El conjunto manchego se llevó los dos partidos sin encajar, 0-2 en Barreiro y 1-0 en el Belmonte, pero aquellas dos victorias cuentan sólo una parte de la historia: los caminos entre Albacete y el filial del Celta se han cruzado muchas más veces, en el césped y en los banquillos. Fran Noguerol volvió al Alba precisamente esa temporada 2011-12 y jugó contra el que había sido su equipo. El gallego acabó siendo capitán de los manchegos. Tras su retirada entrenó al filial, fue segundo entrenador, llegó a dirigir al primer equipo y hoy forma parte del cuerpo técnico. El vigués Rubén Albés dirigió al Celta B entre 2017 y 2019 y al Albacete entre 2022 y 2024. "Uno ha nacido en Vigo, siendo del Celta, yendo al estadio", recordó en alguna ocasión cuando ya entrenaba al Alba. En los dos banquillos coincidió con Agus Medina, que vistió la camiseta del filial celeste entre 2016 y 2018 (68 partidos y 6 goles) y que llegó al Belmonte en el verano de 2023, con Albés en el banquillo. El albaceteño Alfon González, formado en la cantera del Alba, debutó con el primer equipo en Segunda B en 2017 y en agosto de 2020 llegó cedido al Celta B. El club vigués se quedó con él en 2021 y en el filial celeste firmó 92 partidos oficiales y 27 goles, 15 de ellos en la 2023-24, la temporada que le abrió la puerta del primer equipo de Claudio Giráldez. En noviembre de 2024 marcó su primer gol como profesional, ante el Barça, y en el verano de 2025 fichó por el Sevilla. Javi Rueda hizo el viaje en sentido contrario: tras una gran temporada en el Celta Fortuna (2023-24), llegó cedido al Alba en la 2024-25, donde sumó 31 partidos y 4 goles, y regresó a Vigo para hacerse un hueco en el primer equipo, con el que ha renovado hasta 2029. Joseba Etxeberria compareció este sábado con el equilibrio como mensaje. "Es verdad que el equipo está bien, eso nos da confianza, pero a la vez seguimos en descenso y esa necesidad nos tiene que impulsar a dar nuestra mejor versión", advirtió el técnico, que no podrá contar con Higinio, lesionado, ni con Corpas, sancionado, y que esperará a la última sesión para decidir sobre San Bartolomé. El vasco pide un Belmonte lleno pese al horario: "Sabemos que es lunes, sabemos que es una mala hora, pero les necesitamos". Y puso el foco en la tabla: "Sabemos que de conseguir la victoria les empatamos a puntos y eso para nosotros es energía pura". El Celta Fortuna acumula cuatro derrotas seguidas lejos de Vigo y el Alba puede sumar su cuarta victoria consecutiva del campeonato.

articles.title: Las dos caras de Enzo Fernández: “Siempre haré lo que el entrenador me pida”
articles.standfirst: Scaloni sacrifica el rol ‘llegador’ que le otorga Maresca en el City para entregarle las llaves de Argentina
articles.summary: Scaloni sacrifica el rol ‘llegador’ que le otorga Maresca en el City para entregarle las llaves de Argentina
articles.body: Apenas tiene 25 años. Pero Enzo Fernández (Buenos Aires, 2001) puede presumir de ser el tercer jugador que más dinero ha movido a lo largo de la historia. Tan sólo Neymar (400) y Lukaku (376) superan los 310 millones que han generado sus traspasos a Benfica, Chelsea y Manchester City. La sensación, sin embargo, sigue siendo que su mejor versión llega cuando viste la camiseta de Argentina. Recién aterrizado en Europa desde River Plate, se coló en la lista de Scaloni para el Mundial 2022… y acabó siendo elegido como el ‘Mejor Joven’ del torneo. Semanas después, el Chelsea rompió la banca poniendo 121 ‘kilos’ encima de la mesa para sacarlo de Benfica. Hasta la llegada de Morgan Rogers (138) el pasado verano, el fichaje más caro en la historia del conjunto ‘blue’. Con su pase al City, la mayor venta (145) por encima de Hazard al Real Madrid. Aquel Enzo Fernández irrumpió como un centrocampista de base de la jugada con unas dotes innatas para organizar el juego viendo el campo de cara y sacando a relucir su amplio rango de pase. Un perfil que no abunda en la actualidad. Con Maresca, sin embargo, experimentó una ‘mutación’ hacia un perfil más ‘llegador’ que también está replicando a sus órdenes en el Chelsea. “Está mejorando muchísimo. Probablemente en los últimos dos años con nosotros se ha convertido más en un mediocampista ofensivo, antes jugaba un poco más atrás”, explicaba Maresca. “Me parece increíble cerca del área, tanto por sus goles y asistencias como por su liderazgo. Creo que está creciendo mucho”. Los números, desde luego, respaldan la decisión. En 92 partidos a sus órdenes, Enzo ha marcado 17 goles y repartido 20 asistencias. Scaloni, sin embargo, sigue priorizando su rol como ‘cerebro’ en Argentina. El último ejemplo fue en el amistoso ante Uruguay, donde se situó en la segunda altura de un centro del campo completado por Palacios y Mac Allister… con Nico Paz pisando también carril interior a pesar de arrancar como extremo. La diferencia con respecto a su versión en el Manchester City parece que habla de dos jugadores completamente distintos. Y es que, mientras que en la Premier League apenas promedia 46 pases con éxito por partido, frente a la Celeste registró 128: 83/92 en campo propio (90%) y 45/48 en la mitad contraria (94%). Además, ejecutó 6/9 en largo (67%). De hecho, de un cambio de orientación a Prestianni nació el gol de Julián Alvarez. Al final, es una cuestión de encaje en dos estructuras completamente diferentes y, sobre todo, con necesidades distintas. “Siempre haré lo que el entrenador me pida. En la posición que me pidan jugar, daré mi mejor versión. No tengo problema. Lo importante es ayudar al equipo”, aclaraba. Son las dos caras de Enzo Fernández: una con Maresca… y otra con Scaloni.

articles.title: Expediente Steele: dos años sin jugar un minuto en Premier... pero fijo para Tuchel en Inglaterra
articles.standfirst: El portero suplente del Brighton ya estuvo en la lista de marzo y como apoyo en el Mundial
articles.summary: El portero suplente del Brighton ya estuvo en la lista de marzo y como apoyo en el Mundial
articles.body: “Los equipos ganan campeonatos, así de simple. Desde el primer día tuvimos muy claro que nuestro objetivo era seleccionar y formar el mejor equipo posible, lo cual no significa necesariamente seleccionar y reunir a los 26 jugadores más talentosos. Lo que buscamos lograr este verano sólo se puede conseguir como equipo", aseguraba Thomas Tuchel para justificar las ausencias de Foden, Palmer, Maguire y Alexander-Arnold en la lista del Mundial y la sorprendente presencia de Jason Sean Steele (Newton Aycliffe, 1990). El portero del Brighton, que aún no ha debutado con Inglaterra, ya se había 'colado' en la lista de marzo. "Jason es un caso especial porque planeamos llevar a cuatro porteros al Mundial y el cuarto portero tiene un rol especial: es un especialista. Apoyará al grupo de porteros, al entrenador de porteros, al grupo de lanzadores de penaltis y aliviará la carga de trabajo de los demás, por eso necesitamos a alguien con calidad, con experiencia, con la energía y la actitud adecuadas, y creemos que Jason es esa persona. Esto es una especie de prueba para ver cómo funciona este grupo en conjunto para el Mundial", se justificaba 'TT'. Y tan especial. Steele, de 36 'primaveras', acumula más de dos años a la sombra de Bart Verbruggen. Para encontrar su último partido en Premier League hay que remontarse hasta el 24 de agosto de 2024. Desde aquella victoria sobre el Manchester United (2-1) apenas ha disputado 10 partidos, todos en Copas. "No juego todas las semanas en mi club, así que mucha gente se preguntará por qué estoy en la convocatoria, pero entreno duro y me preparo cada día como si fuera a jugar, así que quizás eso tenga un impacto positivo en el grupo. Estoy muy ilusionado con esta oportunidad, espero demostrar mi valía", confesaba el meta. Es curioso. Steele no había tenido ningunta otra experiencia a nivel selección... desde que representara a Gran Bretaña en los Juegos Olímpicos de Londres 2012. "Elegimos a tres porteros más Steele. Quiero aprovechar esta oportunidad para agradecer a Jason por su brillante trabajo y a Brighton por su gran cooperación y apoyo", reiteraba Tuchel tras anunciar la lista para la Copa del Mundo. "He venido aquí para ayudar de en todo lo que que pueda, ya sea dando consejos, apretando en los entrenamientos o quitándole trabajo a los demás. Espero que mi experiencia a lo largo de mi carrera pueda ayudar, aunque sea un poquito. Si sirve para ayudar a alguien y eso contribuye a conseguir un poco de éxito, significará muchísimo para mí. Espero poder aportar energía positiva y buenos niveles de exigencia en los entrenamientos", reiteraba el guardameta. Algo bueno debió hacer. Jude Bellingham le animó a subir al escenario después de que Inglaterra se colgara el bronce y Jordan Henderson le reservó una medalla. No sólo eso. Ante la carestía de porteros ingleses en Premier -sólo Pickford, Trafford, Walton, Rushworth y Henderson son titulares-, Steele repite en la lista junto a Pickford y Trafford. Es más, si por un casual llegara a jugar, se convertiría en el tercer debutante más veterano en la historia de Inglaterra. "No lo he pensado mucho. Creo que, en esta etapa, se trata simplemente de estar preparado para cualquier situación. Y me gusta pensar que lo hago a diario: estar listo cuando me necesiten, entrenar al máximo y jugar bien cuando tenga la oportunidad. Lo más importante para mí es intentar ser el mejor compañero posible, tanto dentro como fuera del campo", insiste. En el Brighton también están encantados con él. "Es un gran tipo y un gran líder para nosotros en el vestuario. Siempre suele hablar antes de los partidos, ya sea dando consejos o intentando animar a los compañeros. Es genial par los jóvenes. Realmente eleva los estándares. Sube mucho el nivel en los entrenamientos y creo que puede ser un gran activo para Inglaterra", apuntaba Jack Hinshelwood. El 'Expediente Steele' continúa abierto.

articles.title: La nueva vida de Gica: "En Slatina pasé de casi morir ahogado con 11 años a ser ahora el 'presi' del club"
articles.standfirst: El legendario jugador rumano ex de la Real, Villarreal y Getafe nos cuenta su proyecto de llevar a Primera a su equipo: "Creo que me parezco más a Fernando Roig que a Laporta o Florentino"
articles.summary: El legendario jugador rumano ex de la Real, Villarreal y Getafe nos cuenta su proyecto de llevar a Primera a su equipo: "
articles.body: Gica Craioveanu (Hunedoara, Rumanía, 1968) ha regresado a la ciudad donde creció futbolísticamente para ponerse como presidente al frente del CSM Slatina. Se implica en los fichajes, defiende que el entrenador tenga siempre la última palabra y sueña con llevar al club a la Primera rumana. Y no olvida que cuando era un niño de 11 años estuvo a punto de morir ahogado en el río Olt de la ciudad que ahora le venera como presidente de su club. Damos un paseo por los alrededores de la Ciudad Deportiva y nos lleva al lugar que nunca olvida porque casi no lo cuenta: "Me cogió un remolino, me lanzó hacia el fondo y como no sabía nadar pensé que me ahogaba. Por suerte, aparecieron de no sé donde dos chicos y me salvaron. Llevo buscándolos toda la vida y a pesar de que lo he contado en radio, prensa y televisión, nunca aparecieron para que les agradeciera con lo que quisieran que me devolvieran la vida", recuerda Gica. En Slatina dio sus primeros pasos en el fútbol y empezó a construir una carrera que le llevaría hasta España, donde se convirtió en uno de los jugadores más queridos por las aficiones de la Real Sociedad, el Villarreal y el Getafe. Décadas después, Craioveanu ha cambiado el césped por los despachos, aunque sin perder su esencia. Vive en Bucarest, viaja a Slatina siempre que puede, trabaja en televisión, colabora en España en radio con Onda Cero y disfruta de una aventura que le permite seguir cerca del fútbol sin soportar la presión diaria de un entrenador. Tiene ambición, proyectos y una idea muy clara de cómo debe funcionar un club. También un sueño: llevar al Slatina a Primera y construir un estadio a la altura de la ciudad. P. No quiso ser entrenador y ha acabado siendo presidente del Slatina. ¿Cómo ha acabado así su historia? R. El año pasado me lo ofrecieron. Me hicieron ciudadano de honor de aquí, de Slatina, donde crecí futbolísticamente. En Rumanía existe la costumbre de que, cuando te nombran ciudadano de honor, te ofrecen un terreno para que eches raíces, como se suele decir. Como no tenían terrenos muy buenos (risas), me ofrecieron ser presidente y no lo dudé ni un segundo. Es algo que me gusta, me motiva. Además, había estado dos años junto a Ángel Torres, en el Getafe, como asesor presidencial. Como no me gustaba ser entrenador, decidí hacerme presidente. P. ¿Cuál es su labor en el club: tomar decisiones o ser una figura más representativa? R. Soy más una figura representativa, pero también me implico en los fichajes y en algunos detalles. Escucho mucho al míster y sus deseos. En Rumanía muchos propietarios son también presidentes de los clubes, se meten mucho en el equipo y toman decisiones. Pero yo, con la cultura española que tengo, no me meto nunca. Para mí, el míster es el número uno. Todo lo que desea y en lo que podemos ayudarle, ahí estamos. También tengo muy buena relación con los jugadores, porque me gusta tenerlos contentos. Cuando los chicos están contentos, el rendimiento es muy bueno. P. ¿Y cómo se maneja en lo de negociar con los representantes y hacer fichajes? R. Eso se cierra con los representantes, por supuesto, pero todo pasa por el entrenador. Si al míster le encaja el jugador y económicamente podemos asumirlo, adelante. Nosotros no podemos permitirnos grandes lujos ni gastar dinero sin control. Intento no firmar, aunque tenga la última palabra, porque no me gusta asumir esa responsabilidad. No creo que sea muy bueno para esos detalles. Creo que en mi teléfono tengo 500 o 750 jugadores y unos 25 representantes de Mozambique, de Bangladesh... (risas) Es lo que hay. Todo lo que recibo se lo mando al míster, porque él busca un perfil determinado de jugador. Si a mí me gusta y a él le encaja, adelante. Pero te digo una cosa: la última palabra sobre el tipo de jugador que queremos siempre la tiene el entrenador. P. ¿Qué futbolistas buscan para el estilo de su entrenador? R. Jugamos con un 4-3-3. Buscamos jugadores jóvenes, con mucha proyección y mucha calidad. Sinceramente, desde que ha llegado el nuevo entrenador hemos mejorado mucho. Antes tuvimos a Claudio Niculescu, que también es ciudadano de honor de Slatina. Fue un muy buen futbolista, un gran jugador en Rumanía, aunque fuera del país no tuvo tanto éxito. P. Imagínese que un día un jugador, incluso la estrella del equipo, viene a hablar con usted para quejarse del entrenador. ¿Cómo reaccionaría? R. Lo escucharía, como escucharía a cualquier jugador. Pero si viene a hablar mal del míster, eso no lo aceptaría. Las cosas tienen que solucionarse entre ellos, tienen que lavarse los trapos sucios en el vestuario. Ahora bien, si hay que tomar una decisión, escuchas siempre a las dos partes, porque nunca uno tiene toda la razón. Además, tengo la suerte de contar con el director general del club, que me ayuda muchísimo. Como viajo tanto y estoy más tiempo fuera que dentro, cuando yo no estoy, es él quien toma las decisiones. P. Buscando un paralelismo con los presidentes del fútbol español, ¿se parece a alguien como Joan Laporta, más dicharachero y extrovertido, o a Florentino Pérez, alguien más serio y formal? R. Laporta es muy vivo, muy hablador, tiene mucha personalidad. No lo sé, pero creo que me parezco más a Fernando Roig. Es un club familiar, muy familiar, y también muy tranquilo. Por eso creo que me identifico más con él. Hago todo por mi club, pero sin hacer mucho ruido. El ruido lo hacen los jugadores con sus resultados. P. ¿Qué es lo que más le gusta y lo que menos de ser presidente? R. Creo que ya no tengo edad para viajar tanto en coche o en autobús. Pero me gusta muchísimo estar cerca de los jugadores, darles consejos y motivarlos. Cuando un futbolista está motivado, su rendimiento es mejor. Intento quedar con los chicos, organizar comidas o cenas con ellos y hacer grupo. Para mí, el grupo es fundamental en el éxito de un equipo. P. En Slatina muchos aficionados le han visto jugar y le consideran uno de los mejores futbolistas de la historia de Rumanía. Incluso puede ser el ídolo de muchos de ellos. ¿Nota ese respeto? R. Me siento querido, arropado y respetado. Para mí, el respeto es fundamental. Yo nunca lo he perdido hacia nadie y espero que tampoco lo pierdan hacia mí. La afición está conmigo, pero sinceramente prefiero que esté más con el equipo que con Gica. Los jugadores necesitan mucho más el apoyo del público que yo. P. ¿Se ve aquí muchos años? R. Sí, me veo aquí retirado, con barba, con mis hijos, que tengan niños... ¿Cómo se llaman? P. ¿Nietos? R. ¡Con mis nietos! Y, ¿por qué no? Y ojalá algún día en el Bernabéu con un puro. P. El club tiene un problema importante: no puede ascender este año por su condición de equipo de la alcaldía. ¿Cree que esta situación se resolverá pronto y que Slatina vivirá años bonitos, con un nuevo estadio y el equipo llegando a Primera? R. Sí, sin lugar a dudas. Ahora estamos haciendo todo el papeleo necesario para poder ascender. En Rumanía existe una ley de la Federación que no permite subir a Primera División a los equipos que pertenecen a la alcaldía. Pero estamos trabajando en un partenariado con varias empresas poderosas de Slatina. La ciudad tiene compañías muy importantes, como Pirelli, y muchas fábricas potentes. De hecho, creo que es la única ciudad de Rumanía que no tiene paro. Con ese grupo de empresas y patrocinadores, el año que viene queremos atacar el ascenso. P. Para eso también necesitan un estadio nuevo. R. No escondo nunca nada, porque soy un tío sincero y digo lo que pienso. Cuando vi el campo, me entró una depresión. Es muy antiguo, está muy mal, porque no se ha hecho nada desde hace 40 años, prácticamente desde que murió Ceausescu. Y eso me duele muchísimo, porque la base es muy buena y tenemos muchos terrenos de entrenamiento magníficos. Pero el estadio, lamentablemente, es feo y está descuidado. P. En España hay mucha gente que le sigue queriendo y que le recuerda con cariño. Las aficiones del Villarreal, la Real Sociedad y el Getafe le tienen muy presente. Además, es comentarista de Onda Cero y de televisión. ¿Cómo es ahora su vida en Rumanía? R. La verdad es que no me lo esperaba, pero tengo una vida muy bonita. Tengo mucho ajetreo. Además de trabajar en Digi, una televisión rumana muy importante en la que damos la Liga española, la francesa, la alemana, la italiana, Fórmula 1 y muchas otras competiciones, soy embajador de una casa de apuestas que se llama Superbet y presidente de este club. Y luego está Onda Cero, que también me llena mucho. La radio es muy amena, me gusta muchísimo y me identifico con ella. P. Lleva 21 años trabajando en la radio española y sigue ligado al fútbol, se le ve feliz, con la misma sonrisa que cuando jugaba. R. Sí, seguro. Cuando era jugador lo decía y lo sigo pensando. Nosotros, los futbolistas, somos 25 tiburones. Lo he declarado siempre y mira mi currículum. Todos pensamos que somos mejores que el de al lado. Nunca he oído a un jugador decir que es peor que otro. Llevar un vestuario es muy complicado, y cada vez lo es más. Por eso intento no mirar a entrenadores como Mourinho o Hansi Flick, que en tres, cuatro o cinco años acaban con el pelo blanco. Demacrados, sí, pero no por feos o por viejos, sino por la tensión, el estrés y la presión de tener que conseguir resultados de la noche a la mañana. Eso no va con mi carácter. Yo soy un tío muy feliz como soy. Soy un cachondo mental, porque lo soy, y para mí eso es lo mejor. En Slatina veneran a Gheorghe 'Gica' Craioveanu. Todos se rinden a su figura: desde el alcalde ("Es el mejor embajador que tenemos en el mundo") hasta el entrenador ("cualquier consejo suyo es oro) pasando por el único español del equipo, Pol Muñoz, al que convenció Gica con una llamada para fichar "porque todo lo que me dijo el presidente se ha cumplido". Varios de los personajes relevantes de esta ciudad industrial charlan con MARCA sobre la figura más relevante de la historia de Slatina. Para el alcalde, Mario De Mezzo, el impacto de Craioveanu trasciende lo meramente deportivo. El regidor tiene claro que la presencia del exfutbolista es el mejor altavoz posible para su municipio: "Creo que su figura es una de las más importantes de Slatina. Está entre los futbolistas más importantes a nivel nacional y para nosotros es un orgullo y un honor que también haya jugado aquí", asegura De Mezzo, quien celebra personalmente que Gica aceptara el cargo. "Su experiencia es muy valiosa, pero su notoriedad y repercusión nacional e internacional contribuyen de manera decisiva al crecimiento de la entidad. La prueba es que ustedes están hoy aquí porque conocen y respetan a Gică; de lo contrario, probablemente ni siquiera sabrían que Slatina tiene un equipo de fútbol". El alcalde defiende el deporte como eje central de su gestión municipal: "El fútbol es el mejor embajador de una comunidad. Aunque Slatina es una ciudad más pequeña y no podemos competir con el presupuesto de las grandes urbes, lo compensamos con la pasión y el corazón que ponemos en ello". En los despachos del club, la apuesta por Craioveanu fue una decisión instintiva. El mánager general de la entidad, Sebastian Noata, recuerda cómo se fraguó su llegada: "Gica es el jugador más representativo que ha tenido Slatina en toda su historia, el futbolista rumano con más partidos en LaLiga, superando los 300 encuentros. Cuando acepté este proyecto, mi primera idea fue rodearme de gente que supiera lo que significa el fútbol. Fue la primera persona en la que pensé y me alegra mucho que aceptara apenas dos segundos después de hablar. Aporta muchísima experiencia y una imagen muy positiva. Los jugadores y el entrenador vienen a Slatina también porque Gica está aquí. Está permanentemente cerca de la plantilla y os podéis imaginar el impacto que tiene en los futbolistas cuando lo conocen". Lejos del perfil distante de los dirigentes tradicionales, Craioveanu ejerce una presidencia de vestuario y sonrisa permanente. Así lo confirma Adrian Dulcea, entrenador del equipo, quien destaca tanto su conocimiento táctico como su calidad humana. "Tener cerca a Gica es enorme. Cualquier consejo suyo es oro por su trayectoria en España", explica Dulcea. "Pero también nos ayuda la persona: un hombre bueno, siempre con una sonrisa, muy positivo y, a la vez, muy directo, que llama a las cosas por su nombre". El técnico pone como ejemplo la reacción del presidente tras un reciente tropiezo deportivo: "Acabábamos de sufrir nuestra primera derrota después de 15 partidos. Es un presidente diferente porque sabe identificar qué hay que solucionar, pero siempre ve el lado positivo. Nada más acabar el partido me dijo: 'Es una pena, pero estamos en el buen camino'. Entiende perfectamente que la derrota forma parte del juego". El magnetismo de Craioveanu ha cruzado fronteras hasta atraer talento formado en España. Es el caso de Pol Muñoz, futbolista catalán criado en La Masia que encontró en Slatina su destino tras pasar por el fútbol italiano. "No le vi jugar en directo, solo en vídeos, pero me habían dicho que era muy bueno", confiesa el joven lateral español de 22 años. "Este es un club pequeño y familiar, y para mí era muy importante que el presidente fuera cercano. Gica me llamó, me explicó el proyecto y fue totalmente sincero, algo que se agradece mucho porque en el fútbol a veces no se cumplen las promesas. Todo lo que me dijo se ha cumplido". Pol, convencido de haber acertado con el paso a la Segunda división rumana, resume el sentir de un vestuario entregado a su presidente: "Me ha gustado salir de casa, conocer nuevas culturas e idiomas, y voy a aprovechar al máximo estos años aquí en Rumanía". Gica es querido allá por donde va, pero en Slatina tiene un lugar muy especial donde se siente como en casa: "Vamos a Marini, que es el sitio donde mejor se come aquí con mi amigo Marius". La gente del pueblo le saluda, se hace fotos y le trata como un ídolo. Es la nueva vida de Gica, ciudadano de honor de Slatina.

articles.title: La era del goleador Oyarzabal
articles.standfirst: Con nueve goles en 2026, puede acabar por tercer año consecutivo como mejor artillero de la selección
articles.summary: Con nueve goles en 2026, puede acabar por tercer año consecutivo como mejor artillero de la selección
articles.body: “Es un espectáculo. No solo por el Mundial que hizo, sino por todo lo que hace cada vez que está con la selección y también en su club, aunque quizá se valore menos. Encaja perfectamente en la idea del seleccionador y en el fútbol que quiere la selección. Tiene gol, trabajo, capacidad de asistencia... ¡Buenísimo!”. Son palabras de delantero a delantero. Y no de uno cualquiera. Es la radiografía que hace David Villa, el máximo goleador de la historia de la selección, con 59 goles en 98 partidos, de Mikel Oyarzabal, el principal artillero de la España que conquistó la segunda estrella en el MetLife de New Jersey. Sus caminos no llegaron a coincidir. Oyarzabal debutó con España en mayo de 2016, cuando Villa llevaba ya dos años alejado del equipo nacional. En septiembre de 2017, cuando Lopetegui recuperó a El Guaje para su regreso y despedida definitiva, en el 3-0 ante Italia, Mikel también se enfrentaba a los italianos, aunque con la sub 21. Y con sus clubes tampoco llegaron a cruzarse. Ahora, con Villa en los despachos del Atlético de Madrid y Oyarzabal como una de las piezas de más valor de la que es la mejor selección del mundo, sus historias se encuentran. Porque el delantero de Eibar suma a lo largo de 2026 nueve goles con la selección. Esa es la misma cifra con la que cerró el año pasado, en el que fue el máximo artillero de España. Como ya sucedió en 2024, entonces con sólo seis tantos, pero con uno que forma parte de la historia sagrada de la selección: el de la final de la Eurocopa ante Inglaterra. Esos nueve tantos que suma el delantero de la Real Sociedad con España le sitúan a sólo tres del mejor registro de un jugador de la selección en un año natural. Obviamente, esa es otra marca que pertenece a David Villa. Máximo goleador español al término de 2006, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011 y 2014, este último compartido con Pedro y Alcácer, El Guaje fijó en 12 goles el techo de un internacional español en un solo año. Y lo hizo en 2008, el año de la Eurocopa conquistada en Viena. El del cambio radical que transformó la historia de España, dejó atrás décadas de desgracias y puso en marcha un ciclo ganador cuya herencia sigue vigente hoy. Villa alcanzó la docena de goles marcando cuatro de ellos en aquella Eurocopa, tres a Rusia y uno a Suecia. Lo hizo participando en 13 de los 16 partidos que disputó España durante ese año. De aquella época data también otro de sus grandes registros: marcar en seis partidos consecutivos con la selección, los cinco últimos de 2008 y el primero de 2009. Ajeno a todo lo que suponen las marcas personales y con el concepto de equipo siempre por delante, Oyarzabal tiene ante sí solo el partido ante Inglaterra para elevar su cifra de goles en 2026. Ausente en Praga, al igual que Lamine Yamal, se le espera para el duelo ante Inglaterra en el Metropolitano. Ausente en Praga a causa del nacimiento de Eneko, su segundo hijo, Mikel recupera el mando de la delantera de la selección. De golpe, De la Fuente recupera a su primer artillero —nueve goles de Oyarzabal en 2026 y 31 en sus 64 partidos con España— y a Lamine Yamal. El extremo comparte con Mikel Merino la segunda posición en el ránking de goleadores españoles del año: cinci dianas cada uno. Lamine, que cuandoacabó el Mundial sólo sumaba el gol ante Arabia Saudí, el primero de España en la ruta al título, fue la gran estrella hace un mes. La primera venta de la Liga de las Naciones la cerró con cuatro goles en cuatro partidos. Merino firmó tres, más los dos de oro que regaló en el Mundial. La selección española afronta el partido que le queda en 2026 con la cuenta de goles marcados en 35 y una media de 2,05 por partido (17 ha jugado). Esa cifra queda muy lejos del mejor registro de la historia de la selección. Ese registro data del año 2009. Entonces, la España de Del Bosque se fue a los 47 tantos en 16 partidos, 2,9 de media y cinco encuentros en los que la selección marcó cinco o más goles.

articles.title: College football winners and losers: How the conference title game races stack up with 2 weeks to go in the 2026 season
articles.summary: The power conferences are doing away with their conference title games in 2027 as the CFP expands. Will the other six conferences follow suit?
articles.body:
Are we three weeks away from the last conference title games in the foreseeable college football future?

With the College Football Playoff 's expansion to 24 teams becoming official on Monday, the four power conferences are doing away with their title games in 2027 as the field doubles. The status of the conference title games in the other six smaller conferences are still unknown. But there's a realistic scenario where few, if any, leagues host conference title games in 2027 and beyond.

With that in mind, here's how the races for this season's conference title games are shaping up with two weeks to go in the regular season. The Big 12, Conference USA, Mountain West, Pac-12 and Sun Belt will play their title games on Friday, Dec. 4. The following day, the American, ACC, Big Ten, MAC and SEC will have their conference championships.

UTSA got a win over North Texas on Saturday night, while Memphis got a win on Thursday night against South Florida. The Tigers have Navy and Temple remaining — they're a combined 3-9 in conference play.

North Texas has games against Tulane and UAB, while UTSA also gets UAB and ends the season against Tulsa. The Blazers will have a lot to say over the final two weeks.

The Hurricanes and Demon Deacons look on a collision course to meet again in the ACC title game. Miami beat Duke at home on Saturday, while Wake Forest trounced SMU to all-but eliminate the Mustangs from ACC contention. Miami beat Wake Forest 33-20 earlier in the season, but the Demon Deacons have won their last four games against ACC opponents by a combined score of 179-35.

Louisville's only hope of getting to the title game is to beat Pitt in Week 12 and have Wake Forest lose its final two games of the season.

We got a lot of clarity in the Big 12 on Saturday night as we said goodbye to Arizona and Oklahoma State as conference title contenders. Texas Tech returned the opening kickoff for a TD against the Cowboys in a display of how the game would go. The Red Raiders beat OSU 52-27.

Utah, meanwhile, got a late 70-yard TD to beat No. 23 Arizona 40-39 well past midnight in all time zones but the Pacific.

The Utes are in the Big 12 title game with a win at TCU in Week 12. If Texas Tech loses a game over the next two weeks and ends up tied at 7-2 in conference play with the Cougars, opponent win percentage will come into play. Tech and BYU do not play each other in the regular season after meeting twice in 2025.

The Bruins moved to 10-0 overall with a 22-14 win over Illinois on Friday night. If Michigan's offense showed it could do anything, then UCLA could be on a serious upset alert in Week 12. But the Wolverines have scored 13 points over their last two games after scoring a lone TD in a loss to Oregon on Saturday.

Indiana took down USC in Grant Wilson's first start at quarterback and has Washington and Purdue remaining. If the Hoosiers win out and UCLA simply goes 1-1, the Bruins will be be playing a road game in Indianapolis for the Big Ten title. If Indiana drops one of its final two games, other teams — namely, Ohio State — can get into the mix.

Everyone else in Conference USA has at least three conference losses, so this one is pretty simple. Wins by the Flames and Gamecocks in Week 12 lock in the title game matchup. The two don't meet in the regular season as Liberty has reeled off nine straight wins after a Week 1 loss to James Madison. Jacksonville State lost Saturday at Western Kentucky to snap a six-game win streak.

Miami (OH) jumped into the mix with a win over Ohio earlier in the week. With five teams in the running for the conference title game, the final two weeks of midweek MACtion should be fun. Toledo and Ohio play in the final week of the regular season, while Western Michigan and Miami play each other on the Tuesday night before Thanksgiving.

North Dakota State is rooting for New Mexico in Week 12. The Lobos visit Wyoming and a New Mexico win could put the Bison and Cowboys in a tie for second place. North Dakota State has the tiebreaker thanks to a head-to-head win. A Wyoming win, meanwhile, guarantees the Cowboys a spot in the MWC title game since their conference schedule is over after Week 12.

New Mexico lost Saturday at home to UNLV, but has a 21-16 win over North Dakota State in its pocket and plays Air Force in Week 13.

The Bobcats are emerging as the primary challengers to Boise State after wins over Oregon State and Fresno State. Boise State beat Oregon State 46-41 on Saturday night and clinched a spot in the conference title game as a result. Texas State is a game ahead of everyone else, and also lost 46-45 to Boise State just two weeks ago.

The Bobcats' other loss came to the Aztecs, who beat Utah State on Saturday night. But SDSU gets Boise State in Week 12.

We're down to four teams for two spots in the SEC title game. After beating Missouri on Saturday, Georgia is in the title game with a win over South Carolina in Week 12. The Gamecocks didn't have LaNorris Sellers in a loss to Arkansas on Saturday night.

If Alabama, Tennessee and Texas all finish 7-2, the Tide win the tiebreaker on conference opponent win percentage. Tennessee has the head-to-head win over Alabama and Texas has the head-to-head win over Tennessee, but Texas and Alabama didn't play each other. If there's a two-way tie between Alabama and Texas, the Tide still have the tiebreaker thanks to stronger opponents.

The Sun Belt is the only conference in college football that still has divisions. That makes it relatively easy. Louisiana Tech has already clinched the West Division. The Bulldogs are two games ahead of Louisiana and beat the Ragin' Cajuns. In the East, James Madison has the head-to-head win over Georgia Southern, but is still a game back of the Eagles. GSU has Troy in Week 12 and then plays Louisiana Tech in Week 13. JMU is off in Week 12 and has Coastal Carolina on Nov. 28.

Here are the rest of this week's winners and losers.

UConn: The Huskies took a massive step toward bowl eligibility on Saturday and can say they beat a CFP team in the process. UConn beat James Madison 46-22 thanks to three passing TDs from QB Kalieb Osborne and two rushing scores from RB Cyncir Bowers. Osborne was 16-of-20 passing for 274 yards, while Bowers rushed 25 times for 123 yards. UConn has games against Old Dominion and at Wyoming to finish the season. At 5-5, the Huskies just need a split to get a 13th game.

Kansas: Can you believe that Kansas was the first Big 12 team to really slow down West Virginia? The Jayhawks held the Mountaineers to their lowest-scoring game of the season in a 37-14 win. It wasn't turnover-induced, either. West Virginia entered Week 11 averaging 263 rushing yards per game. Saturday, WVU ran 37 times for 35 yards. QB Michael Hawkins carried the ball 25 times for 36 yards. RB Cam Cook had nine carries for 12 yards. Kansas, meanwhile, rushed 55 times for 296 yards and five scores.

Colorado: Deion Sanders has been saying for weeks that his team hadn't quit despite five losses in its last six games. Friday night's performance backed up Sanders' comments. The Buffaloes took down No. 14 Houston 42-32 thanks to 35 points over the second and third quarters. Colorado rushed 39 times for 249 yards and four different players scored rushing touchdowns. That included QB Kaneal Sweetwyne, who had to make a brief appearance thanks to Isaac Wilson's ankle injury. The Buffaloes are now 4-6, and their last two games of the season against Cincinnati and UCF suddenly look a lot more winnable.

UAB: As we mentioned above, the Blazers are in the American title game race thanks to three wins over their last four games. Saturday, UAB beat Temple 36-10 to move to 6-4 overall. The win guarantees a bowl game for UAB for the first time since 2022, when the Blazers went 7-6 under interim coach Bryant Vincent.

Texas A&M: Aggies fans who wanted Marcel Reed to be benched got their wish late in Saturday's loss to Tennessee. Brady Hart came on for Texas A&M's final possession in the 22-7 loss. However, the drive ended when Hart threw an interception himself.

That's how it's going for the Aggies this season. Reed was 9-of-22 passing for 71 yards and a pick, while Hart had two completions for 22 yards to go along with the interception. Texas A&M has lost four straight SEC games since beating Arkansas and scored 43 points across those games. Twenty of those points came against Alabama.

It's ugly in College Station as A&M is now 4-6 with games remaining at Oklahoma and against Texas. At this point, wouldn't the entire fan base trade a 5-7 season for a win over the Longhorns?

Cincinnati: The Bearcats' recent performance is why Colorado will be confident when it heads to Ohio in Week 12. Cincinnati lost its third straight game on Saturday in a 41-13 drubbing at Iowa State. Cyclones RB Aiden Flora ran wild in the first half as he totaled 216 yards and scored three first-quarter touchdowns. Cincy RB Cole Tabb did what he always does with 16 carries for 165 yards, but the Bearcats' passing game was basically nonexistent and Cincinnati also went 1-for-5 on fourth downs.

NC State: It wasn't as bad as the Week 2 collapse against Vanderbilt, but NC State gave away another game Saturday. The Wolfpack lost 34-31 at home to Syracuse despite leading 31-20 with 6:55 to go and immediately getting the ball back with an Orange three-and-out.

The game flipped when CJ Bailey was intercepted by defensive lineman Tunmise Adeleye, who returned it 18 yards for the score.

Syracuse's 2-point conversion failed, but the Orange got the ball right back by forcing a three-and-out themselves. Syracuse then went on a nine-play, 49-yard drive after an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty on the punt put the Orange across midfield, and a Steve Angeli pass to Justus Ross-Simmons with 48 seconds to go was the game-winning score.

Wisconsin: The Badgers faced a Maryland team with an interim coach and a backup quarterback. They lost 24-21. Terrapins QB Cardell Williams rushed for two scores and threw for the game-winner with 2:11 to go as the Terps won their fourth game of the season. Wisconsin freshman QB Ryan Hopkins was 11-of-22 passing for 77 yards and the Badgers had just 102 yards on 31 attempts. At 6-4, Wisconsin is going bowling. But the optimism following the school's home win over USC has disappeared.

articles.title: No. 2 Utah stays undefeated with 40-39 win over No. 23 Arizona
articles.summary: The Utes are 10-0.
articles.body:
The No. 2 Utes (10-0) got a 40-39 win at No. 23 Arizona thanks to a go-ahead 70-yard TD pass from Devon Dampier to Creed Whittemore with 2:35 to go.

The throw came just after Arizona (7-3) took a 39-33 lead with 3:13 remaining after a five-play drive that spanned 91 yards thanks to a 59-yard pass to Isaiah Mizell.

After Whittemore's TD, Arizona's chance to get a game-winning field goal never got across midfield. Heck, the Wildcats didn't even get a first down. After a completion short of the sticks on third down, Arizona hurried to the line on fourth down to get a play off before the 2-minute warning. Noah Fifita's pass fell incomplete.

Dampier finished 13-of-25 passing for 204 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. He also rushed 14 times for 100 yards and two scores. RB Daniel Bray had 18 carries for 197 yards and a score while filling in for Wayshawn Parker.

Parker started the game and had one carry before not returning because of a heel injury suffered against BYU.

The two teams combined for 48 points in the second half after Utah led 17-14 at halftime. Arizona scored 10 points off Utah turnovers in the second half thanks to a fumbled pitch on the first play of the second half and a muffed punt in the fourth quarter.

However, that fumbled punt only turned into a field goal with 8:09 to go. Instead of taking the lead with a touchdown, Arizona simply cut Utah's lead to 33-31.

Fifita was 27-of-43 passing for 356 yards and three touchdowns and an interception. The Wildcats fell to 4-3 in the Big 12 and are out of the Big 12 title mix with losses to the Utes, BYU and Texas Tech — the three teams ahead of them in the standings.

Utah, meanwhile, can clinch a spot in the Big 12 title game with a win at TCU in Week 12.

The game, initially scheduled to kick off at 7:30 p.m. ET, began three hours later because of the FAA ground stop on Friday . Utah's travel was delayed as flights were grounded across the country and the Utes were unable to get to Tucson until Saturday morning.

articles.title: Yahoo Top 10: Utah stakes claim to No. 1 spot with thrilling late-night win
articles.summary: On a mostly quiet Saturday, the Utes delivered a drama-filled late-night win.
articles.body:
College football delivered a mostly quiet day Saturday.

It was Sunday that brought the mayhem — real early Sunday, when Utah survived a scare from Arizona, 40-39 , in the desert in a game that kicked off at 10:30 p.m. ET Saturday.

The Utes remained undefeated — only one of two in the country (UCLA) — after doing just enough in the final quarter Saturday in Tucson, keeping them in the top spot in our Top 10.

But let's get back to that ho-hum Saturday. Sure, Maryland upset Wisconsin (is Luke Fickell's job back in jeopardy?); Dabo Swinney's Clemson team lost at home to previously 2-7 Georgia Tech; and Wake Forest — Wake! — throttled SMU in a victory that pushed them up in our Top 10. But otherwise, there was a lot of the expected that materialized a day after the unexpected — a four-hour airplane ground stoppage across the country .

Perhaps it would have been better for USC to stay home in LA. Indiana likely popped the Trojans' playoff bubble. Also in the Big Ten, Oregon rolled Michigan in what's shaping up to be a season of horribles for the Wolverines, and Iowa continued to keep alive its playoff hopes (you never know!).

In the SEC, Georgia reigns supreme, Kentucky's magical season took another blow from Florida, and Tennessee (Texas A&M), Alabama (Vanderbilt) and Texas (LSU) survived ugly road games to stay in position for the postseason. In the ACC, Wake and Miami seem headed toward the championship game in Charlotte.

Meanwhile, in the Group of Six playoff chase, Boise State outlasted Oregon State in a 46-41 duel in Idaho, and UNLV upset New Mexico and coach Jason Eck. The Broncos are in the G6 playoff driver's seat.

The Utes needed some late-game heroics on offense and defense to survive in a tight one in the desert. QB Devon Dampier ran for 100 yards and threw for more than 200 yards and Daniel Bray had the game of his life — amassing 197 yards rushing. Utah and coach Morgan Scalley didn't arrive in Tucson until around 12:30 p.m. on Saturday after the flight ground stoppage on Friday forced cancellations. It mattered not on this night.

The Bulldogs seem awfully angry since their stunning home loss to Auburn on Oct. 17. Kirby Smart's team outscored its next three opponents 117-36, including a whopping 48-21 win over Missouri on Saturday. QB Gunner Stockton threw for 252 yards and the Bulldogs had two rushers eclipse 65 yards in the win. The defense stymied a Missouri offense that converted 18 percent of its third downs.

Nursing a tight lead in a Friday night game, the Bruins managed to stop Illinois, driving for the tying score, twice: one on downs and the other on an interception that they turned into a field goal. Ty Dieffenbach rebounded from an in-game shoulder injury to throw for two touchdowns and Wayne Knight ran for a tough 56 yards. WR Aidan Mizell had a second straight 150-plus receiving day, too.

Backup QB Grant Wilson, a seventh-year senior, threw for more than 300 yards and two touchdowns in leading the Hoosiers over the Trojans. While Wilson is one of the best stories going in college football, IU's defense was the real hero on Saturday. They came up clutch with an interception and fumble recovery in the fourth quarter to secure the win.

Any letdown from the Irish's emotional victory a week ago against Miami was quickly dismissed. The Irish led 31-0 at halftime in an all-around complete whipping of the Eagles. Notre Dame RBs Jonaz Walton and Nolan James Jr. combined for more than 210 yards and two scores. If the Irish are going to win playoff games, they'll need that rushing attack to stay nasty.

The Hurricanes erupted in the second half to turn a three-point lead at the break into a romping victory with its two high-profile Duke transfers leading the way in beating their former team. Former Blue Devils players Cooper Barkate and Darian Mensah connected eight times for 134 yards. Mensah carved through his ex-teammates, completing 30 of 41 attempts as Miami rebounded from the loss at Notre Dame in impressive fashion.

Not paying attention to the Demon Deacons? Better start. Jake Dickert, surely to be a hot name in the coaching cycles (his new contract isn't gonna stop the offers), has Wake Forest roaring. The Deacs were up 42-0 at one point and completely suffocated the Mustangs to the tune of 275 total yards. Wake QB Gio Lopez ran for 34 yards and two TDs, threw for another and wasn't even needed much in the second half.

It was far from pretty, but the Crimson Tide defense led the way in this one, smothering the Commodores to the tune of 12 rushing yards and a 13% clip in third-down attempts. Despite its two losses, Alabama has put itself in position for a top four seed in the 12-team playoff and a first-round bye. With the kind of defense displayed on Saturday in Nashville and shifty QB Keelon Russell, perhaps Bama can make some noise in the postseason.

Arch Manning threw three interceptions. But he also tossed the game-winning touchdown in the final seconds of his first-ever college game in his home state. The win keeps the Longhorns' playoff hopes alive. Thank the Texas defense, which picked off Sam Leavitt three times and held LSU coach Lane Kiffin's offense to three three-and-outs in four fourth-quarter drives.

Iowa's path to the playoffs seems very much clear: beat Illinois and Nebraska to end the season and you're in (probably). The Hawkeyes have recovered from the losses to Minnesota and Ohio State by outscoring their last three opponents 82-17. They've got something cooking with QB Hank Brown, who scored a touchdown through the air and on the ground and had just nine incompletions against the Boilermakers.

articles.title: El Barça pierde el control de Araujo
articles.standfirst: La última palabra sobre su futuro la tienen el Liverpool y el propio jugador
articles.summary: La última palabra sobre su futuro la tienen el Liverpool y el propio jugador
articles.body: La Dirección Deportiva del Barcelona anda buscando un central en el mercado. El rendimiento de la defensa no ha sido el esperado por Flick, como ha quedado patente en algunos partidos, y busca refuerzos con el fin de afrontar la segunda parte de la temporada. Era algo que se podía prever. Deco estuvo mucho tiempo buscando un central para reforzar el equipo en verano, pero, a la hora de dar el paso definitivo para fichar, Flick decidió descartar su incorporación. No solo eso. El Barcelona también perdió a Ronald Araujo. El uruguayo se marchó cedido al Liverpool y dejó al equipo con cuatro centrales. Un número que, a priori, puede ser suficiente, pero, teniendo en cuenta el historial de lesiones de Christensen, era una medida un tanto arriesgada, tal y como ha quedado demostrado después de que el danés haya tenido que estar un mes más de baja. Araujo está rindiendo a un excelente nivel en Anfield. Iraola le ha dado confianza y está ofreciendo su mejor versión, si bien es cierto que está jugando más como lateral que como central. Pero lo está haciendo muy bien, la afición está encantada con él y la Dirección Deportiva del Liverpool estudia seriamente hacer efectiva la opción de compra que tiene sobre el jugador para el próximo verano. Lo sorprendente es que el Barcelona no contemple el regreso de Araujo al club, ya sea ahora, en el mes de enero, o pensando en el futuro, de cara al verano. El motivo, básicamente, es que no puede hacer cábalas sobre su regreso porque es algo que ya no depende de él. Si el Liverpool quiere hacer efectiva la opción de compra y Araujo está de acuerdo —y todo hace indicar que así es, porque se encuentra feliz—, el Barcelona no tendrá ninguna opción de recuperarlo. Así lo establece el contrato que han firmado ambas partes. Si el Liverpool paga los 55 millones de euros que cuesta dicha opción, el Barcelona no podrá hacer nada para recuperar al uruguayo, salvo intentar convencer al futbolista de que no acepte la oferta de los ingleses. Algo muy complicado después de lo sucedido en el Barcelona y de su actual situación en Liverpool. Araujo ha sorprendido a todos. Nadie esperaba un rendimiento tan bueno y, sobre todo, de una manera tan inmediata, ya que no ha necesitado ningún periodo de adaptación. El charrúa está destacando desde el primer día, tanto a nivel defensivo como ofensivo, ya que ha marcado un par de goles en estos primeros meses. El Liverpool estaría dispuesto a comprarlo ahora mismo, pero la opción de compra solo se puede ejecutar a final de temporada. Además, tampoco tendría sentido hacerla efectiva ahora, porque el rendimiento del jugador podría bajar en los próximos meses o podría sufrir una lesión. Está claro que el Liverpool no comprará al futbolista hasta final de temporada, si es que finalmente decide hacerlo.

articles.title: Reality dawns after Wales dared to dream
articles.summary: As Welsh rugby fans wake up on Sunday morning the realisation will dawn on them that Wales beat New Zealand for the first time in 73 years.
articles.body:
Did that really happen? Or was it just a dream?

As Welsh rugby fans wake up on Sunday morning the realisation will dawn on them.

It has happened. Wales have finally beaten the All Blacks again.

For the first time in 73 years - after 34 defeats - 19 December, 1953 is now joined by 14 November 2026 as a defining date in Welsh rugby history.

Thousands of young kids will this morning be turning up to rugby training or matches, driven by parents who have a hint of a headache, with this magical day fresh in the memory.

Steve Tandy's heroes will always have this moment, with inspirational captain Dewi Lake and player-of-the-match James Botham shedding tears.

"Best day of my life," concluded Wales centre Eddie James.

It was a result that sent shockwaves throughout Wales but also around the sporting world.

Friends and relatives who had not been in contact for ages messaged each other to revel in or discuss the result.

People reminisced that their parents or grandparents never saw this day.

There was jubilation in Cardiff but also disbelief at the timing and magnitude of the occasion.

Welsh rugby has been in disarray since the end of the 2023 World Cup after so many of the golden generation retired.

The Wales men's national team slumped to a record 18 straight Test defeats in a winless run that lasted 16 months as the side slipped to a lowest world ranking of 14th.

Tandy had only won four tests in 13 matches, those victories coming against Japan twice, Fiji and Italy. His side had been hammered twice by world champions South Africa without scoring a point and conceding 116.

So when they awoke on Saturday morning hardly anybody outside the camp would have thought this Welsh team would succeed where previous Grand Slam winning sides had failed to topple New Zealand.

There had been hope, even occasional expectation, before previous contests. That was generally not the feeling this time around, as Wales - ranked 10th in the world - took on a New Zealand side that were ranked top before kick-off in Cardiff.

So where does this staggering result stand in Welsh rugby history?

There have been some wonderful days, with Grand Slam successes clinched in Cardiff in 1976, 1978, 2005, 2008, 2012 and 2019.

Then there was the 30-3 drubbing of England in Cardiff in 2013 to clinch the Six Nations title, while Warren Gatland's side defeated the same opponents two years later at Twickenham in the World Cup.

But this is New Zealand. The All Blacks. A Wales win an achievement many thought might never happen again.

Some might question people for celebrating a victory against a New Zealand side that had rested some top players. You will not find many of those in Wales today.

"I have never seen a performance like that from the men in red," said Radio Wales commentator Cennydd Davies.

"They have emptied the tank and created history."

Tandy has created history by becoming the first Wales coach to beat New Zealand.

Wales had no head coach when they defeated the All Blacks in 1905, 1935 and 1953, with David Nash the inaugural appointment in 1967.

Tandy has succeeded where World Cup winning coaches Sir Graham Henry and Steve Hansen failed by masterminding a Welsh success against New Zealand.

Welsh Grand Slam winning coaches like Gatland, Clive Rowlands, John Dawes and Mike Ruddock also could not inspire the feat Tandy has now achieved.

The unassuming man from Tonmawr has had a tough initiation in his first 15 months as an international head coach but has now announced his arrival on the Test stage.

Tandy has had to deal with questions over his selections and coaching style, but nobody could ever question whether he has the backing of the squad or the way he has immersed himself in the job.

Players often reference the way Tandy keeps in touch, whether they are based in Wales or ply their club trade in England.

This squad play both for each other and for Tandy. There was no greater evidence of that than on Saturday.

Tandy has also finally been provided with a permanent back room staff. It is reaping the rewards.

Tandy earned his international stripes as a defence coach with Scotland and the British and Irish Lions.

The arrival of Peter Murchie, who is in his second campaign as defence coach, is starting to pay dividends with former Wales flanker Dan Lydiate providing able support.

Nothing portrayed the evidence of Welsh players commitment to the Tandy cause than the superhuman defensive effort of the final quarter.

Official rugby statistics are often hard to pin down, especially defensive ones.

Different sites produce slightly differing numbers that are often modified over time when games are analysed again.

The official Nations Championship chart confirmed Wales made a record tally of 346 tackles.

Lock Dafydd Jenkins tops the charts at 38, which matches the tally set by France captain Thierry Dusautoir against New Zealand in the 2007 World Cup quarter-final at the same Cardiff ground.

Jenkins was followed by Jac Morgan (31), Botham (30), centre Eddie James (25) and Lake (24).

Wales had the top nine tacklers on the field, with replacement prop Gareth Thomas making 19 in just 26 minutes.

Defence is not built on statistics alone.

The heart and desire was evident in a final quarter where Wales did not concede a try, and New Zealand captain Beauden Barrett remarked afterwards the All Blacks felt they had hit a brick wall.

A final quarter in which the All Blacks were held up over the Welsh line on three occasions following major interventions from flankers Botham and Morgan and replacements Thomas and Dan Edwards.

A final quarter in which James provided a remarkable try-saving tackle and replacement number eight Taine Plumtree secured two vital turnovers.

Traditionally, the All Blacks have eased away in these closing stages. Not on this occasion.

This was a victory for guts and glory, summed up by BBC rugby correspondent Chris Jones who said: "These results don't happen in international rugby these days.

"It can happen in football where you get an early goal and then it's backs against the wall and you win 1-0.

"In rugby, teams are too powerful and well-drilled, the superior side normally prevails, the resistance eventually breaks and the dam bursts.

"But that didn't happen in Cardiff. The Welsh defence was heroic."

Attack matches defence in five-star display

The remarkable rearguard resistance is what will live long in the memory, but Wales' victory was also built on the clinical offensive game most evident at the start of each half.

Wales were never behind in the game as they held leads of 14-0, 21-7 and 35-21.

That was thanks to tries from Tomos Williams and Lake within the first six minutes of the game and a couple more from centre James and Louis Rees-Zammit at the start of the second half.

Prop Archie Griffin also popped up with a score as Wales crossed for five tries, the most they have scored against New Zealand in Cardiff.

The attacking orchestrator was scrum-half Williams, who enjoyed one of his finest games for Wales, with his long passing repertoire in full flow.

Williams was ably assisted by half-back partner Sam Costelow, who has had to endure criticism during his short international career in Wales' most high profile jersey.

Fly-half Costelow answered those doubts with an assured performance and also kicked beautifully with five conversions.

Rees-Zammit and New Zealand born full-back Blair Murray continually stretched the All Blacks defence, while centre James proved he is a Test match performer.

Attack coach Matt Sherratt will be a happy man this weekend.

A footnote to the day was that the game was played in front of 55,152, the lowest attendance for this fixture at the Principality Stadium.

It was 13,000 fewer than 12 months ago with almost 20,000 empty seats on show.

The fans that stayed away missed out on a magical afternoon as the players produced a performance worthy of a full stadium.

Those in attendance made themselves heard with Barrett stating it felt like New Zealand were facing 16 or 17 players.

"Since I've been here, I've loved what the crowd brings," said Tandy.

"I believe we've got the best stadium in the world and it is inspiring for our players and supporters being part of that.

"It is what it is. We had 50-odd thousand here but we've got to perform and hopefully we can grow that.

"I see what the boys do in the communities also and how they connect to our people."

Whether this attracts people to Cardiff next Saturday for a late match against Australia (20:10 GMT) remains to be seen.

Welsh rugby has been divisive in recent years that it was always going to take a remarkable result like this to provide an opportunity to bring opposing factions together.

Welsh rugby's issues will not be solved by one win.

articles.title: 'It's more like a knockout match!' – Mark van Bommel issues passionate rallying cry ahead of Italy showdown
articles.summary: Belgium head coach Mark van Bommel has described his side's crucial UEFA Nations League encounter against Italy as a high-pressure knockout match. Van Bommel...
articles.body:
Belgium head coach Mark van Bommel has described his side's crucial UEFA Nations League encounter against Italy as a high-pressure knockout match. Van Bommel stressed that victory is essential as the Red Devils fight for quarter-final qualification in Brussels.

High stakes in Brussels for Van Bommel's men

Belgium return to home soil in Brussels to face Italy at the Koning Boudewijnstadion knowing that victory is essential to secure a top-two finish in UEFA Nations League Group 1. Mark van Bommel's side currently sit third in the standings following an inconsistent campaign, though they bounced back from a heavy defeat against France by securing a vital 2-1 win over Turkey.

With a fierce three-way tussle for quarter-final qualification reaching its climax, the Red Devils are gearing up for their biggest test yet.

Van Bommel's preparations have been slightly disrupted, having to manage without injured pair Leandro Trossard and Mike Penders.

Van Bommel demands elite mentality under pressure

Speaking ahead of the crunch fixture, Van Bommel emphasised that his squad must fully embrace the immense pressure , comparing the encounter directly to sudden-death tournament football.

"Victory is all that matters. It's not a final, but this is about whether we advance to the next round or not; it's more like a knockout match," Van Bommel stated.

The Belgian manager believes that experiencing this level of intensity is invaluable for the squad's development ahead of future international tournaments.

Assessing Italy's rapid evolution under Mancini

Van Bommel also acknowledged the significant tactical transformation Italy have undergone under Roberto Mancini since the reverse fixture earlier in the campaign.

"It's an interesting test to play under pressure, especially in view of major tournaments. We always prepare the same way, whether it's a final or not," Van Bommel noted.

Praising their upcoming opponents, he added: "It's a different Italy to the one we met in the opening match. They're more solid and have improved in a short time. You don't beat France by chance, and their victory didn't surprise me."

Red Devils target quarter-final berth on home soil

As the group stage reaches its dramatic conclusion, Belgium know that securing maximum points against a resurgent Italian outfit is the only guarantee of advancing to the next round.

The tactical battle at the Koning Boudewijnstadion will test Van Bommel's setup to its absolute limits as they look to exploit home advantage.

Belgium are fully focused on delivering a disciplined, statement victory in Brussels to book their place in the Nations League quarter-finals.

articles.title: “Time to Find Somebody Else”: Frustrated Keyshawn Johnson Has Had Enough of Lincoln Riley After USC’s Loss to Indiana
articles.summary: Lincoln Riley is facing mounting pressure following USC’s 27-13 loss to the Indiana Hoosiers. The defeat effectively ended the Trojans’ (7-3, 4-3 Big 10) pla...
articles.body:
Lincoln Riley is facing mounting pressure following USC's 27-13 loss to the Indiana Hoosiers. The defeat effectively ended the Trojans' (7-3, 4-3 Big 10) playoff hopes.

Keyshawn Johnson posted a video on X expressing his disappointment with the loss and calling for Riley's firing.

"I tried my best, but in all honesty, it's time to find somebody else," he said . "I'm sorry, man. I don't even know what to say. Where did we go wrong? It's unbelievable. I don't even know what to say. I guess, 'Fight On.'

USC struggled to turn its offensive production into points, managing just 13 despite recording 409 total yards. Quarterback Jayden Maiava went 26 of 42 for 311 yards, with one touchdown and three interceptions. Indiana quarterback Grant Wilson, on the other hand, went 17 of 27 for 305 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception.

The Trojans have two games left, against Maryland and UCLA, but winning both may not be enough. The defeat has intensified scrutiny of Riley, whose five-year tenure has yet to produce a College Football Playoff appearance or a conference title. Reports earlier this season suggested USC could consider moving on from Riley depending on how the campaign finished, although his estimated $70 million buyout remains a major obstacle.

Lincoln Riley Believes in Himself as USC HC

After the loss, Lincoln Riley reaffirmed his belief in himself and his desire to continue leading the program. Riley stated that he still believes in the process and remains hopeful about the future.

"I believe in what we're doing. I believe in myself," he said, per On3 . "I believe in our leadership. I believe in our administration. I believe in everything that's happening here. Trust me, there's nobody that wants it as bad as all of us involved."

Riley said the Trojans showed that they could put up a good fight, which only reaffirmed his belief in the team.

articles.title: Arch Manning shakes off 3 interceptions, throws game-winning TD pass as Texas beats LSU
articles.summary: As he has been throughout his college football career, Texas quarterback Arch Manning was a mixed bag on Saturday.
articles.body:
As he has been throughout his college football career, Texas quarterback Arch Manning was a mixed bag on Saturday. But Manning and Texas came out on top.

After throwing three interceptions and seeing his team fall behind LSU 21-10, Manning turned it on late, culminating in a 12-play, 58-yard drive that saw Manning throw the game-winning touchdown pass with three seconds remaining as Texas won 22-21.

"That's what college football is all about," Manning said after the game.

Manning's numbers were not impressive: 19-of-35 for 174 yards and one touchdown with three interceptions and four sacks, plus 35 yards and a touchdown running. But when Texas needed him to march the offense down the field at the end of the game, he did it. His touchdown pass to Raleek Brown was a perfectly placed ball, and he also ran for two first downs on the game-winning drive.

For No. 6 Texas, the win means they'll almost certainly be in the College Football Playoff, as they'll be heavy favorites the next two weeks against Arkansas and Texas A&M. For LSU, the loss knocks first-year coach Lane Kiffin out of playoff contention.

Manning, the scion of the first family of quarterbacks, will have an opportunity do what neither his grandfather Archie nor his uncles Peyton and Eli ever did: Win a national championship.
