articles.title: Un 7 saca otro 7
articles.standfirst: Mientras llora aún la grave lesión de Barrenetxea, la Real se ilusiona con la confirmación, tras su golazo 'maradoniano', de que Dani Díaz es una promesa hecha realidad
articles.summary: Mientras llora aún la grave lesión de Barrenetxea, la Real se ilusiona con la confirmación, tras su golazo 'maradoniano', de que Dani Díaz es una promesa hecha realidad
articles.body: Con el dolor aún presente por ver a Barrenetxea en una camilla después de ser operado de una lesión que le puede tener de baja lo que resta de curso, y la emoción que fue ver como Kubo le dedicaba el gol que marcó con Japón, el jugador que comparte posición y número en el Sanse, Dani Díaz, firmó uno de los goles de la temporada y se postuló como opción para suplir en la Real Sociedad al donostiarra. Al menos, hasta que vuelva. Si dicen que un clavo saca otro clavo, igual un 7 saca otro 7. El importante problema muscular de Barrenetxea dejó a Pellegrino Matarazzo sin uno de sus principales atacantes y con sólo Take Kubo, Gonçalo Guedes y Job Ochieng como extremos en su plantilla. Los dos primeros, en baja forma; y el tercero, recién llegado a la élite. Como apuntamos en MARCA, antes de mirar al mercado de enero, la Real debía recurrir a Zubieta, como en teoría manda su filosofía, y ahí había una opción por encima de las demás. Y es que Dani Díaz, internacional en categorías inferiores y hace dos veranos campeón de Europa sub 19, se está saliendo este curso, en el que ya ha igualado las 14 titularidades del pasado y casi los minutos. Fichado hace seis años del Racing de Santander, en esta campaña está cumpliendo con las altísimas expectativas que había en torno a él, siendo una pesadilla para todos los rivales, protagonizando innumerables jugadas de peligro y dejando un golazo ante el Andorra, cuando recibió un balón pasado el medio campo y, tras regatear a dos contrarios, mandar la pelota casi por la misma escuadra. El cántabro había estado cerca de marcar más veces, pero el sábado en Zubieta se desquitó cuando hizo uno de los tantos del curso en todas las categorías, al coger el balón al borde del área propia y llegar a la contraria tras irse por velocidad y calidad de los rivales que le salieron al paso y batir al portero del Sporting de disparo raso, cruzado y ajustado a palo. La denominada jugada 'maradoniana' o 'messianica' en su máximo esplendor, pese a que su ídolo sea Cristiano y por ello lleve el 7. Fue, probablemente, uno de los mejores goles que se han visto en la ciudad deportiva txuriurdin, por la que en su día destacaron sobremanera Oskitz Estefanía, Javi De Pedro, Jose Javier Barkero o los mismísimos Mikel Oyarzabal y Ander Barrenetxea. Un selecto grupo de futbolistas talentosos a los que se ha unido Dani Díaz, que ha tirado la puerta y ha pedido a gritos una oportunidad como la que tuvieron ellos. Y encima el siguiente partido de la Real es en su Cantabria natal. Este cuento no parece haber acabado y puede tener aún un final más feliz.

articles.title: Polls open in Cape Verde in race with first female presidential candidate
articles.summary: Joana Rosa and four other opposition candidates face off against President Jose Maria Neves, who wants a second term.
articles.body:
Voters have begun casting their ballots in Cape Verde, where President Jose Maria Neves is facing off against the West African island nation’s first female presidential candidate, Joana Rosa, in a vote hinging on slowing down persistent emigration.

More than 300,000 people are eligible to vote on Sunday from 8am to 6pm (09:00 GMT to 19:00 GMT) and will choose from six presidential candidates in a country known for its stability in the politically volatile region.

Neves, a member of the country’s oldest political party, the African Party for the Independence of Cape Verde (PAICV), is tipped to be the favourite but faces his strongest challenger in Rosa of the Movement for Democracy party.

The 66-year-old served as prime minister for 15 years and became president in 2021. His party won 37 of 72 parliamentary seats in May, allowing Neves to appoint Francisco Carvalho, then mayor of the capital, Praia, as prime minister.

Rosa, an opposition candidate and former justice minister, is the first woman to run for president since independence in 1975. Her party governed for 10 years before the May vote.

The country runs a hybrid parliamentary-presidential system of government that sees the president enjoy veto authority and a mediating role.

Cape Verde, a tourism haven located off the coast of Senegal, gained global fame this year after its men’s football team battled with much bigger nations to reach the World Cup knockout stages. In April, a cruise ship sailing off its coast was struck by a hantavirus outbreak.

Emigration has long been a problem because of a dearth of jobs. The archipelago has more people living in the diaspora than the 500,000 people residing on its islands. Most are in Portugal, its former coloniser, and the United States.

Nearly 77,000 diaspora Cape Verdeans are registered to vote at embassies abroad.

Neves has promised to organise a youth summit to address emigration if he is elected to a second term. Rosa, meanwhile, called for a government that allows young people “to build their futures here at home and prevent the continued exodus of young Cape Verdeans abroad”.

But many voters feel distant from the political class over concerns that it doesn’t understand their daily difficulties, Roselma Evora, a professor of political science and gender studies at the University of Cabo Verde, told The Associated Press news agency.

Results are expected within two to three days.

Candidates must clinch more than 50 percent of the vote to win, or the top two candidates will face a run-off vote on November 29.

articles.title: Men's Rugby League World Cup final - Australia 32-12 New Zealand: Kangaroos brush off Kiwis to win fourth straight world title
articles.summary: Australia reigned supreme as they successfully defended their world title for the fourth consecutive time, as they beat New Zealand 32-12 in the men's Rugby League World Cup final
articles.body:
Australia had begun the tournament slowly, narrowly beating New Zealand 24-22 in their World Cup curtain-raiser in October, but when it came to the business end of the World Cup, they showcased why they are the best team in the world.

It ushered in another era of dominance for Australian Rugby League, after the Jillaroos also completed a four-peat of World Cup victories, following their 34-10 victory against New Zealand's women's side earlier on Sunday.

New Zealand had been out to win their first World Cup since 2008, but James Fisher-Harris' side were errant in defence, missing 37 tackles as Reece Walsh and Bradman Best tore apart the Kiwi line.

"I can't put it into words. It's unbelievable," player of the match, Bostock, said.

"We were written off early in the tournament, and probably didn't play our best games.

"Last week, you saw us start to turn it on, we saw glimpses of what we could do, and today we put it all together on the big stage.

"We've got 10 club captains in our team, so there's so much leadership.

"If I can just pick up stuff from them in my young career, it's only going to do me good. I'll never forget this day."

The Kangaroos wasted no time in getting on the scoreboard, with Martin, carrying three New Zealand defenders, driving over inside 95 seconds of kick-off.

New Zealand have been in excellent form throughout the campaign, and despite going down early, they hit back ten minutes later with Casey McLean receiving a chest pass from Kodi Nikorima, before darting over from close range.

The hosts made them pay, with Walsh and Best showcasing their elite handling skills to flick the ball out to Bostock, who crossed over in the corner for his first of the match.

Best then added his name to the scoresheet as Australia continued to ruthlessly probe their way through the Kiwi's defensive line.

Tom Dearden sucked in multiple defenders before sending the ball out wide to Best, who wrong-footed another defender before darting through a big gap to score.

Martin and Tom Trbojevic would bookend tries either side of half-time, with the Penrith Panthers back-row again crashing over from 10m out.

Walsh then left New Zealand stunned, dancing his way around multiple defenders before popping the ball off to Trbojevic, who scored three minutes into the second half.

New Zealand began to grow into the match, with Ronaldo Mulitalo having a try chalked off for a knock-on in the build-up before Isaiah Papali'i gathered a grubber kick from Nikorima to get a try back with 14 minutes to go.

But Australia were ruthless, with Bostock taking a sublime back-hand offload from Best in the corner to score his second, and secure Australia's men's 13th Rugby League World Cup.

New Zealand full-back Kalyn Ponga explained he was gutted by the loss but accepted his side were second best.

"It's pretty disappointing," Ponga said to Channel 7.

"We set a goal at the beginning of the camp, spoke about it at length, and it was just a disappointing performance.

"Credit to them, they played a better style of footy, and we made too many errors.

"It's disappointing because we worked so hard and built throughout the weeks for this moment, but it didn't come together."

Tedesco confirms international retirement

James Tedesco had initially been named as a reserve for tonight's match, but after Latrell Mitchell was forced to pull out due to illness, the Sydney Roosters full-back was drafted into the squad.

He explained that he hadn't even expected to come off the bench during Sunday's match, before adding that he was set to retire from international rugby league.

"I didn't expect to be playing or getting any minutes, but Kevvie gave me the last five minutes; to be part of it is pretty special," Tedesco said.

"Whatever my role with this group was, I was happy with. This will be my last time wearing this jersey, so it was pretty special.

"We talked from the start about what we were building. There were a few questions asked about our group, but I think we saved our best for last."

articles.title: Pelea en el Calcio por Mastantuono: Milan, Roma y Nápoles preguntan y la Fiore quiere retenerlo
articles.standfirst: El argentino es un fijo en el esquema viola y su futuro ya es motivo de debate en la Serie A
articles.summary: El argentino es un fijo en el esquema viola y su futuro ya es motivo de debate en la Serie A
articles.body: Franco Mastantuono ha renacido en la Serie A. El argentino aterrizó con 19 años, y tras un traspaso superior a los 60 millones de euros, en el Real Madrid, y se fue difuminando hasta perder todo el protagonismo en una campaña compleja para el cuadro blanco. Con el aterrizaje de Mourinho se apostó por una salida a préstamo y la Fiorentina fue el destino elegido por todas las partes para que el chico siguiera evolucionando en Europa. En el primer tercio de temporada, la apuesta se ha confirmado como un acierto. 11 partidos como titular en Serie A y cuatro goles le han convertido en un fijo en el esquema de un cuadro viola que ya comienza a moverse para intentar retenerle durante más tiempo. El diario La Repubblica asegura que la Fiorentina pretende ampliar la cesión de Mastantuono un curso más, aunque advierte de una condición clave: el equipo toscano necesita pelear por entrar en Europa para facilitar la operación y convencer al futbolista. El buen desempeño de Mastantuono ha provocado que más clubes italianos se interesen por su situación. Varios medios transalpinos reportan que equipos como Milan, Roma y Nápoles ya han sondeado al entorno del argentino para conocer las condiciones que se tendrían que asumir para enrolar al atacante en su proyecto. El tiempo dirá qué ocurre con Mastantuono, pero la certeza a estas alturas de la temporada es que su cesión en Italia le está sentando de maravilla y ha disparado su confianza. Otra cosa muy distinta es si tendrá hueco en la futura plantilla del Real Madrid a sus 20 años. De momento, el plan de los blancos con su joven apuesta argentina sigue su curso.

articles.title: Arsene Wenger will not stand against Gianni Infantino for Fifa presidency
articles.summary: Arsene Wenger decides against running for the Fifa presidency, in a boost to Gianni Infantino's hopes of a fourth term.
articles.body:
Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger has decided not to stand against Gianni Infantino as a candidate in Fifa's presidential election.

The Frenchman had been considering running for the job but sources have told BBC Sport that he has ruled himself out.

Current world football chief Infantino's position was plunged into crisis by a backlash caused by his failed plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Wenger - who is Fifa's head of global development - would have had the backing of European football's governing body Uefa, which has spearheaded opposition to Infantino.

On Saturday, French newspaper L'Equipe reported that Wenger was unlikely , external to challenge his boss.

Wenger has credibility throughout the footballing world, and this will be a significant boost to Infantino as he seeks a fourth term as president.

Uefa is said to still be hopeful of finding an alternative candidate before Wednesday's deadline.

One influential figure in the group of stakeholders opposed to Infantino told BBC Sport the news was "a real shame".

"Even if not perfect, I do think he could have galvanized many around the world," they added.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October.

Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also announced his intention to stand.

However, sources have told BBC Sport that the 68-year-old has not yet secured the necessary five endorsements from member associations ahead of Wednesday's deadline but is "still fighting hard".

Amid the fallout over FFE, Wenger, who has traditionally been loyal to Infantino, distanced himself from the aborted plot.

"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports," Wenger said at the time.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity."

Infantino has retained support in South America, Africa and Asia, and recently insisted he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football.

articles.title: Beltrán Capote, el todoterreno que conquista Valdebebas
articles.standfirst: El joven talento llegó al Real Madrid hace dos temporadas procedente del Málaga para cumplir su sueño de vestir de blanco
articles.summary: El joven talento llegó al Real Madrid hace dos temporadas procedente del Málaga para cumplir su sueño de vestir de blanco
articles.body: Beltrán Capote no ha necesitado demasiado tiempo para hacerse notar en Valdebebas. El joven futbolista atraviesa un momento de crecimiento en la cantera del Real Madrid y sus números así lo reflejan. Esta temporada suma 13 goles y 10 asistencias, después de cerrar la anterior con 23 tantos y 20 pases de gol. Unas cifras que hablan de su capacidad para aparecer cerca del área, marcar diferencias y participar de forma directa en el juego ofensivo de su equipo. Nacido en Doña Mencía (Córdoba) y afincado desde muy pequeño en Rincón de la Victoria (Málaga), allí comenzó a construir el camino que acabaría llevándolo hasta el Real Madrid. Su progresión llamó la atención del club blanco, que lo incorporó hace dos temporadas. Para Beltrán era mucho más que un cambio de equipo. Suponía cumplir el sueño que había perseguido desde niño. La ilusión por vestir de blanco pudo con todo, aunque la decisión también tuvo una parte difícil. Tuvo que dejar atrás Málaga y separarse de su familia para instalarse en la residencia del club. En Valdebebas ha continuado desarrollando un perfil que destaca por su versatilidad y su facilidad para llegar al gol. Siempre ha jugado en el centro del campo, aunque ha pasado por distintas posiciones durante su formación. Empezó como mediocentro organizador, también actuó de interior y llegó a jugar en banda, hasta asentarse como mediapunta. Ahora destaca por su capacidad para dar el último pase y aparecer en el área, con buen golpeo y facilidad para convertir sus llegadas en goles. Su entorno lo define como un futbolista “todoterreno”, una descripción que encaja con su recorrido sobre el campo. La relación de Beltrán con el Real Madrid, en cualquier caso, viene de mucho antes de su llegada a la cantera. En marzo de 2015, cuando todavía no había cumplido seis años, visitó por primera vez el Santiago Bernabéu junto a sus padres. Su padre había reservado en secreto una comida en el Real Café, desde cuyo comedor se veía el interior del estadio. Al llegar, el pequeño solo quería entrar y hacer el tour. No tenía ninguna intención de sentarse a comer, hasta que vio el campo desde la mesa. Entonces cambió de idea. “¡No, no, no! Nos quedamos, nos quedamos a comer”. Primero disfrutó de aquella comida con sus padres y después recorrió el estadio. Más de una década después, aquel niño que no quería perder un minuto antes de entrar al Bernabéu trabaja para hacerse un sitio en el club con el que siempre soñó.

articles.title: Livakovic se arma de paciencia
articles.standfirst: Asegura en declaraciones a la prensa croata que está a la espera de su oportunidad
articles.summary: Asegura en declaraciones a la prensa croata que está a la espera de su oportunidad
articles.body: Dominik Livakovic se encuentra estos días concentrado con la selección de Croacia, disputando los partidos de la Nations League. La selección de su país está encuadrada en el mismo grupo que España, pero no se ha clasificado para los cuartos de final, a diferencia de Inglaterra y del combinado de Luis de la Fuente. En su país sorprende que el portero titular de Croacia no juegue con el Barcelona. Sin embargo, Livaković se lo toma con calma. Es consciente de la dificultad que supone ocupar la portería del Barcelona, que cuenta actualmente con Joan García como guardameta titular. "Juego en el Barcelona, soy un chico de Zadar y estoy realmente muy orgulloso de ello. Ya he defendido la portería de un club tan grande. Entreno, espero mi oportunidad y me encuentro bien", declaró el portero en rueda de prensa. También destacó el nivel de los entrenamientos que se llevan a cabo en el club azulgrana, algo que ha podido comprobar desde que llegó al equipo el pasado verano: "Los entrenamientos en el Barcelona son realmente duros porque estamos hablando de los mejores jugadores del mundo. Sería ideal que pudiera jugar todos los partidos, pero espero mi oportunidad con paciencia". Livaković ha disputado un partido con el Barcelona. Fue frente al Sevilla y lo hizo porque Joan García se encontraba lesionado. De momento, es consciente de que está por detrás del guardameta español, pero sigue esperando su oportunidad.

articles.title: Billy Vigar: Pitch perimeter rules under review after player's death
articles.summary: The Premier League, English Football League and Women's Super League are reviewing pitch perimeters after the death of Billy Vigar last year.
articles.body:
The Premier League, English Football League and Women's Super League are reviewing pitch perimeters across their clubs in light of the death of former Arsenal academy player Billy Vigar last year.

Vigar died at the age of 21 from a "significant brain injury", five days after colliding with a concrete wall surrounding a pitch while playing for non-league side Chichester City.

On the eve of this season the Football Association banned clubs from having concrete, breeze block or solid brick walls surrounding their pitches, but this only applied to the National League and Women's National League.

Now it has emerged there is work under way at the highest levels.

It is understood the Premier League carried out a survey of clubs on pitch perimeters, including on the material used and the run-off distance, in light of Vigar's death.

The top flight also shared the outcome of the FA's review with clubs.

BBC Sport has approached the Premier League for comment on the outcome of its pitch survey.

The EFL also issued a survey to clubs at the start of this year to build a picture of the perimeter structure at each ground.

This also sought information about run-off distances, surfaces and gradients, and any other trip hazards.

BBC Sport understands specific health and safety assessments have been recommended for clubs found to have high-risk perimeters, in order to mitigate risk.

This survey was in addition to the regular work carried out at the beginning of the 2025-26 season, and came as a result of Vigar's death.

Meanwhile, in the WSL and WSL2 there is an acknowledgement that many of the grounds are shared with men's teams in other leagues.

The police investigation into Vigar's death is ongoing, with a further hearing scheduled for 10 February.

The Metropolitan Police expects there will be another "two to three months" before any conclusion is reached.

Vigar's parents, Keith and Camilla, told BBC Sport on the one-year anniversary that "the FA could have stopped Billy losing his life because they had so many warnings".

BBC Sport is investigating incidents involving pitch perimeters at all levels of football in England and Wales. If you have been affected by any such incident, please contact us.

articles.title: Hendon's first match since death of Ezekiel Williams abandoned because of serious injury

A match involving a team playing for the first time since the death of one of their players was abandoned because of a serious injury.

Non-league Hendon were returning to action for the first time since midfielder Ezekiel Williams, 26, died in hospital on 2 November from head injuries after an incident in Milton Keynes.

Saturday's game at Bedfont Sports in the Isthmian League South Central Division was abandoned within 10 minutes after Hendon defender Ethan Creary was carried off on a stretcher and taken to hospital.

A Hendon statement read: "Early signs are that he's suffered a double break to the collarbone, possible shoulder ligament damage and concussion."

Hendon posted a picture of Creary , external in hospital wearing his kit with a message from the player.

"I have to be in the ward for 24 hours to assess any potential bleed in the brain. It's just protocol and I woke up feeling OK," Creary said.

Before Saturday's game, players from Hendon and Bedfont Sports observed a minute's silence for Williams.

articles.title: Highlighting Heisman Front-Runners to Watch in 2026 Race After Week 11
articles.summary: The 2026 Heisman Trophy feels like it's Jeremiah Smith's award to lose.
articles.body:
The 2026 Heisman Trophy feels like it's Jeremiah Smith's award to lose.

The Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver produced his sixth 100-yard receiving game of the campaign on Saturday to move back into the role of Heisman favorite at FanDuel Sportsbook.

Smith is favored ahead of a handful of quarterbacks, including Darian Mensah of the Miami Hurricanes.

Mensah and others aren't out of the race yet, but they need to string together a few more impressive outings to contend with the resume that Smith has put together.

Jeremiah Smith recorded 11 receptions, 117 receiving yards and a touchdown on Saturday against the Northwestern Wildcats.

Smith extended his scoring streak to seven games, had a double-digit reception total for the fourth time this season and eclipsed the 100-yard mark for the sixth time in 2026.

Smith is either first or second in the FBS in receptions, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns.

He is the best pass-catcher in college football and arguably the best individual talent in the sport.

Smith should be able to run up the statistics next week against the Nebraska Cornhuskers.

His last big test will come against the Michigan Wolverines in two weeks. A strong game from Smith in the rivalry clash should finish off the Heisman-winning campaign.

If he struggles against Michigan, that might leave the door open for a quarterback to win the Heisman.

Darian Mensah threw for his second-highest passing-yard total of the season against his former team on Saturday.

The Miami Hurricanes quarterback put up 382 yards, in his second game without Malachi Toney, against the Duke Blue Devils.

Mensah finished Week 11 in the top 10 in the FBS in passing yards and touchdown passes.

He has 3,076 passing yards, 29 touchdowns and just two interceptions.

Mensah has two home games against the Virginia Tech Hokies and Boston College Eagles to pad his final regular-season numbers. Miami is expected to be a huge favorite in both of those games.

The ACC Championship Game is the highest-profile game left for Mensah, but even that will feature a Miami team as a massive favorite.

If Smith does slip up in any capacity, Mensah seems to be the guy to take over for him as the Heisman favorite. At minimum, the Miami quarterback should be a Heisman finalist.

Devon Dampier has led the Utah Utes to an undefeated season and the No. 2 spot in the AP Top 25.

He doesn't have the overwhelming stats that Mensah has, but it's worth giving credit to him for leading the Utes to a 10-0 record.

Dampier put up 204 passing yards and ran for another 100 yards in Utah's latest win over the Arizona Wildcats.

He's now had at least 250 total yards in Utah's three games against ranked opposition, all of which have occurred in the last month.

Just like Smith and Mensah, Dampier has two easy games left on the regular-season schedule against the TCU Horned Frogs and West Virginia Mountaineers.

Dampier will have the biggest conference championship stage of the top Heisman contenders, though, since Utah will face either the BYU Cougars or Texas Tech Red Raiders in a top-15 battle in the Big 12 Championship Game.

articles.title: 'Cheat Code' Jeremiah Smith Shutting Down Season Addressed by NFL Insiders Ahead of 2027 Draft
articles.summary: Jeremiah Smith is the best player in college football and the Heisman Trophy favorite, per FanDuel Sportsbook, and isn't going to quit on the season just because Ohio State has three losses and is on the outside of the College Football Playoff picture looking in at this point.
articles.body:
Jeremiah Smith is the best player in college football and the Heisman Trophy favorite, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and isn't going to quit on the season just because Ohio State has three losses and is on the outside of the College Football Playoff picture looking in at this point.

Dane Brugler of The Athletic called the wide receiver a "cheat code" and reported there was some speculation Smith might sit out the rest of the season following the Buckeyes' third loss so he could prepare for the 2027 NFL draft. But it became clear during Saturday's win over Northwestern that isn't happening.

"That just isn't how Smith is wired," Brugler wrote. "He cares too much about his teammates and legacy, and that competitiveness fuels his dominance."

Seeing how Smith is a candidate to be the No. 1 overall pick of the draft, perhaps some wouldn't be surprised if he shut things down. However, there is still plenty on the table, including the chance to win the Heisman Trophy and even sneak back into the CFP race.

Ohio State entered Saturday's game No. 20 in the CFP rankings, but No. 11 Kentucky, No. 14 Houston, No. 17 South Carolina, No. 18 USC, No. 21 LSU, No. 22 Missouri, No. 23 Arizona and No. 25 Oklahoma State all lost. The Buckeyes will surely move up in the next set of rankings with two weeks remaining for more chaos to unfold.

They, of course, need to keep winning, and they did that Saturday by targeting Smith early and often against Northwestern.

"I counted 17 targets for the draft's No. 1 prospect, as Ohio State wisely peppered him with passes," Brugler wrote. "The offense is limited with a true freshman quarterback, especially downfield (Smith dusted a corner on one post-corner route, but Luke Fahey's throw was off target). However, Smith consistently got open in the short-to-intermediate game."

Smith also further cemented his place in history by becoming the Big Ten's all-time receiving yards leader:

"He put the entire offense on his back again Saturday, especially in the first half, and just refused to let Ohio State's recent slide continue," Nick Baumgardner of The Athletic wrote. "He's had more impressive days as a college player, on bigger stages, against better competition. But this was quintessential Jeremiah Smith.

"You could point to some of those big days from Ohio State's Playoff run during his true freshman year or his 206 yards against Iowa earlier this season. If you had to use one game to describe Smith, though, this one would at least be on the list. It was a tremendous effort when his team really needed it."

Smith is still on the field for the Buckeyes and will likely remain there unless they are playing in a bowl game outside of the CFP.

And that is bad news for opposing defenses.

articles.title: 15-Year-Old Football Player Dies After Collapsing During High School Gym Class
articles.summary: Levi Curry, who was a freshman and football player at Eagle River High School in Alaska, died at 15 years old.
articles.body:
Levi Curry, who was a freshman and football player at Eagle River High School in Alaska, died at 15 years old.

Jayce Bertrand of KTUU Alaska noted Curry collapsed while playing football in gym class.

Curry's parents, Mary and James, said he was born with a heart condition that was "basically healed" by a previous surgery, per Bertrand.

Curry was an offensive lineman at the school.

"I think 17 years now, and I've never had a ninth-grader start for varsity, especially on the offensive line," football coach Jonathan Wetzel said, per Bertrand.

"... There was plenty of times that I could be having a bad day at work, and I could get to the ball field, and you know see him coming up and his smile would just kind of wash that bad day away."

Curry's funeral happened Wednesday, and approximately 500 people attended.

articles.title: Zidane afronta su primera 'final': "No pienso en el fracaso"
articles.standfirst: 'Les bleus' están obligados a ganar a una Turquía ya descendida a la Liga B para no ver peligrar su clasificación a los cuartos de la Nations League
articles.summary: 'Les bleus' están obligados a ganar a una Turquía ya descendida a la Liga B para no ver peligrar su clasificación a los cuartos de la Nations League
articles.body: Las primeras 'turbulencias' no han tardado en llegar a la nueva Francia de Zinédine Zidane. Tras la derrota sufrida contra Italia, la última jornada de la fase de grupos ante Turquía adquiere un tinte de final en su objetivo por meterse en los cuartos de final de la Nations League. Mbappé, recuperado tras ser baja en San Siro. "No estoy decepcionado. Lo que necesitamos analizar es por qué no estuvimos a nuestro máximo nivel. No fue un mal partido. Pero hay cosas que mejorar", reconocía Zidane después del partido a modo de autocrítica. "A los jugadores les dije que no hay que entrar en pánico y que la derrota no fue totalmente merecida". La situación, desde luego, se ha vuelto bastante delicada... cuando habían dejado la clasificación bastante encarrilada durante el parón de septiembre-octubre. Francia llegaba como líder del Grupo 1 de la Liga A con tres puntos de ventaja sobre Italia. Sin embargo, la derrota en Milán le otorgó la primera plaza a los de Roberto Mancini al tener ganado el enfrentamiento directo. De este modo, Francia está obligada a ganar frente a una Turquía que todavía no ha puntuado en esta Nations League y está matemáticamente descendida a la Liga B si no quiere tentar a la suerte. Por detrás, Bélgica marcha a un sólo punto de distancia. Por tanto, Zidane y todo su 'staff' también tendrán un ojo puesto en Bruselas. Todas las opciones están abiertas para 'les bleus': finalizar como líderes de grupo; meterse en cuartos de final como segundos; o quedar tercero y, por tanto, no avanzar a las eliminatorias. "En ningún momento he pensado que mañana podamos fracasar. Sabemos lo que tenemos que hacer: terminar el trabajo y clasificarnos", decía Zidane. No son pocos los contratiempos en forma de lesión que ha sufrido Zidane desde que comenzó el parón: Kalulu, Tchouaméni y Marcus Thuram tuvieron que marcharse de la concentración por problemas físicos... mientras que Upamecano y Doué también han causado baja tras el partido contra Italia. Tampoco estuvo disponible Mbappé por unos problemas físicos. El atacante del Real Madrid, sin embargo, se ha apuntado a esta 'final' ante Turquía... a quien ya marcó en el partido de ida justo en la acción en la que acabó lesionado. "Su presencia lo cambia todo". Desde su debut con Francia en marzo de 2017, sólo en dos ocasiones se ha encuentros consecutivos. La primera, en 2019, por unos problemas en el muslo; la otra, en 2024, por decisión técnica de Deschamps. Con Mbappé de vuelta, queda por ver cómo reconfigura Zidane su tridente ofensivo... puesto que, en varias ocasiones, ya ha reiterado que quiere jugar con Kylian en izquierda. Por tanto, Barcola podría repetir como '9', a pesar de que se le vio bastante incómodo, o darle la alternativa a un Eli Junior Kroupi que ya debutó en San Siro. No es la única cuestión a la que debe atendar 'Zizou'. Sobre el papel, Konaté debería ser quien acompañe a Jacquet en el eje de la zaga... mientras que todas las miradas apuntan al lateral derecho tras el desempeño de Malo Gusto ante Italia. Reiteró, eso sí, que no se plantea reubicar a Zaïre-Emery. "Si juego, será en el centro del campo". Francia se la juega.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin LSU Contract Buyout Details After Loss to Arch Manning, Texas and Top-10 Losing Record
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin's first season as LSU's head coach is not going as hoped, and now the head coach's contract is under the spotlight.
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin's first season as LSU's head coach is not going as hoped, and now the head coach's contract is under the spotlight.

The Tigers dropped to 6-4 overall and 3-4 in SEC play with Saturday's stunning 22-21 loss to Arch Manning and Texas. Manning found Raleek Brown for a touchdown in the final seconds to put the Longhorns ahead for good and all but eliminate LSU from the College Football Playoff race.

If LSU did decide to move on from Kiffin, it would be a costly move.

Biggest Coaching Buyouts in College Football History 💰

ESPN's Adam Rittenberg reported in December 2025 he agreed to a seven-year, $91 million deal and noted that LSU would owe him 80 percent of his remaining salary should it fire him. What's more, that amount is "not subject to offset or mitigation, according to the term sheet," although it features a buyout that would start at $7 million and drop to $6 million in January 2027 if he left for another head coaching job.

While moving on from Kiffin so quickly would be shocking, it is fair to start asking questions given his overall struggles against quality competition.

Morgan Moriarty of Sporting News noted Saturday's loss dropped him to 6-19 against top-10 foes and 15-28 against ranked teams as a head coach for Tennessee, USC, Florida Atlantic, Ole Miss and now LSU.

Stewart Mandel of The Athletic didn't exactly paint a pretty picture in his description either.

"LSU fans, on the other hand, must be wondering whether there's an out clause in Kiffin's $91 million contract," Mandel wrote. "The Tigers have faced four current Top 25 teams (No. 3 Alabama, No. 6 Texas, No. 11 Kentucky and No. 19 Ole Miss) and lost to all four. (No. 8 Tennessee is next.) Not a great look for anyone, but especially someone who makes $13 million a year, routinely knifes his employers, struts into stadiums with a celebrity entourage, appears in TV commercials and had a near-$50 million roster to play with this season. His hand-picked portal QB, Sam Leavitt, got picked off three times by Texas' Jelani McDonald (two of them in the end zone) and has a national-high 12 on the season.

"Meanwhile, every time ABC showed Kiffin on the sideline, he looked nervous and in pain. A far cry from the cocky guy who used to throw his play sheet in the air when he knew he'd just called a touchdown. Like perhaps the pressure of trying to avoid a fourth loss of the season at a place that fires national championship coaches is getting to him. But this is what LSU signed up for—hot yoga, hot celebrities … and a 6-19 career record against top 10 foes."

The losses have at least been close for LSU outside of an 18-point defeat to Alabama.

It went back-and-forth with Ole Miss throughout the game until the Rebels scored the go-ahead touchdown with fewer than seven minutes remaining. And Kentucky defeated Kiffin's team by one point after successfully scoring a two-point conversion in overtime.

It seemed as if LSU was going to defeat Manning and Co. on Saturday with an 11-point lead in the second half, but the Longhorns controlled the closing stretch and then left with a shocking victory in the final seconds.

Ultimately, it was more of the same for Kiffin against a quality opponent. That means he will be under plenty of pressure during the 2027 season to turn things around from what is shaping up to be a disappointing first campaign with the Tigers.

articles.title: You are the Scotland boss - what would you do?
articles.summary: Put yourself in the shoes of Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli as he picks his starting XI for the visit to Switzerland.
articles.body:
Scotland delivered a first home win under Sebastien Pocognoli on Friday but a stodgy 2-1 against North Macedonia did little to lift the frustrated mood of fans.

Now the Nations League campaign concludes with a visit to runaway group winners Switzerland.

Scotland must win in St Gallen to have any chance of leapfrogging Slovenia into second place and the promotion play-offs.

It will also determine their seeding for the impending Euro 2028 draw. Falling into pot three less than a year after topping a World Cup qualifying group would be a huge backward step.

So is it time to let the shackles off and go for broke or would it be more prudent to adopt a defensive strategy and hope to sucker the Swiss on the break or from a set-piece?

Put yourself in Pocognoli's shoes and pick an XI with our team selector below, while we have picked out some of the key selection dilemmas.

Pocognoli has settled on a 3-4-2-1 formation but the approach is far from convincing, with a lack of threat from the flanks among the issues facing the Belgian.

On the left, there are question marks about the quality of Andy Robertson's deliveries in recent times. On the right, natural winger Ben Gannon-Doak has looked entirely uncomfortable.

Would it be more effective to use them in their regular club positions? Pocognoli has intimated that he is not married to the system, telling BBC Scotland he will try "to find the best shape to make the players shine on the pitch.

"I always try to adapt to my team. I think the shape that we play is the best shape to fit the best quality of the team."

If he is going to stick with three at the back, does Kieran Tierney perhaps have a better delivery than Robertson? Is a three at the back system the only way to accommodate both?

Either way, Robertson is going to start and he's going to become the nation's most capped player.

Full-backs Aaron Hickey and Nathan Patterson are certainly more used to defending than Gannon-Doak, but can they be relied upon to provide a cutting edge in the final third?

On a largely-exasperating evening, Gannon-Doak did earn the penalty that brought victory on Friday. If the boss sticks to his guns, could his speed and direct running be utilised behind a striker instead of out wide?

Six goals to go - will McGinn catch Dalglish & Law?

Tough watch as Scotland again battle against their own limitations

Che Adams was reinstated straight into the starting line-up by Pocognoli after missing the new head coach's first international window through injury.

While he didn't get on the scoresheet, his subtle bump on a North Macedonian defender led to John McGinn's first goal and his combination play with Scott McTominay was noticeable.

Hull City striker Oli McBurnie started the first four games of the Pocognoli era after ending his long exile from the squad and earned praise for his industry, but he remains without an international goal.

However, it was McBurnie who was chosen to replace Adams after 66 minutes with Kieron Bowie left on the bench and Robbie Ure omitted from the matchday squad.

Could his slightly more robust approach be a better foil for the likes of Scott McTominay and John McGinn?

Or will Pocognoli stick with Torino striker Adams, who has four goals in nine Serie A games this season?

Speaking of Serie A Scots, Bologna midfielder Lewis Ferguson has played every single minute under Pocognoli - the only outfield player to achieve that feat.

Billy Gilmour has started next to Ferguson in midfield in all of five of those games, with the head coach keen for the Napoli man to play a little higher up the pitch instead of in the deep-lying role he played under Steve Clarke.

Again, there have been questions about the effectiveness of the pair. Ferguson was arguably Scotland's best player in a poor World Cup display and his ball-winning prowess might suit the Switzerland game.

But no player in the English Premier League has won the ball back more in the opposition half than Ryan Christie.

The former Inverness, Aberdeen and Celtic midfielder was more known for his attacking intent but over the last 18 months, he has been moved to a deeper, more central role in a flying Bournemouth team.

He recently captained the Cherries to a 3-0 win over AC Milan, has started of three of the last four in Bournemouth's unbeaten league run, and began in the 3-0 win over McGinn's Aston Villa in the League Cup.

He reached his 75th cap coming off the bench against North Macedonia but has started just once under Pocognoli, in the 2-1 loss against Slovenia.

Is there a place for him in this team? Who would drop out if that were the case? Or is there a way for Pocognoli to name all five big midfielder - including McGinn and McTominay - at once?

articles.title: Tenerife play first game since death of striker Jesus de Miguel
articles.summary: Tenerife play their first game since the death of striker Jesus de Miguel on an emotional day at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium.
articles.body:
Tenerife played their first game since the death of striker Jesus de Miguel on an emotional day at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium.

De Miguel died at the age of 30 on 3 November, a day after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a home match in Spain's Segunda Division.

Tenerife beat bottom side Ceuta 2-0 on Sunday, with tributes to De Miguel paid both before and during the game.

Lengthy standing ovations preceded and followed a minute of silence before the match.

In the ninth minute play was stopped and a round of applause took place, while a video of De Miguel was shown in the stadium, as happened at all first- and second-tier games in Spain last weekend.

Tenerife fans displayed a banner that read: "Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally blue and white."

Forward Nacho Gil opened the scoring for the home side in the 40th minute and celebrated by holding up De Miguel's shirt.

Gil revealed a message written under his shirt that read: "Demi, always in our hearts."

Neal Viereck scored four minutes from time as Tenerife ended a run of six games without a win. They are 14th in the table.

Tenerife's game with Granada on 7 November was postponed and the club invited fans to the stadium to pay their respects to De Miguel.

Owono was given a 12-match suspension by the Spanish football federation for the challenge which resulted in De Miguel's death.

The federation has ruled that the game between Tenerife and Andorra, which was abandoned seven minutes into stoppage time after the incident occurred, will not be replayed and the 2-2 score will stand.

articles.title: Lincoln Riley's USC Contract Buyout Info amid Hot-Seat Buzz After Loss vs. Indiana
articles.summary: The No. 18 USC Trojans saw their College Football Playoff hopes shattered in a 27-13 loss against the No. 9 Indiana Hoosiers on Saturday.
articles.body:
The No. 18 USC Trojans saw their College Football Playoff hopes shattered in a 27-13 loss against the No. 9 Indiana Hoosiers on Saturday.

The loss cast a spotlight on USC coach Lincoln Riley's tenure with the team.

Riley signed a 10-year, $110 million contract with the Trojans in 2021. That deal gave him considerable job security, especially since a midseason firing would be financially difficult. If Riley were to be fired this season, USC would owe him a $70 million buyout .

After the loss to Indiana, Riley expressed confidence in his ability to turn things around.

"Absolutely," Riley said. "I believe in what we're doing. I believe in myself. I believe in our leadership. I believe in our administration. I believe in everything what's happening here. And trust me, there's nobody that wants it as bad as all of us involved. And we know how close we are as a group, we know how close we are as a team, and we got a good view of that tonight. So we're going to keep battling. We will get there and all this will continue to make it more sweet when that time does happen."

Despite being equipped with a top-end roster, the Trojans have lost three game and their lone victory against a ranked team came against the struggling No. 20 Ohio State Buckeyes.

When USC president Beong-Soo Kim was asked in October about potentially firing Riley, he offered a short response.

"We're not thinking about that," Kim said. "We are laser-focused on the next game, and then the game after that."

That line of thinking may have changed as pressure and scrutiny have continued to mount. Former USC wide receiver Keyshawn Johnson was among those calling for Lincoln to be fired after USC's most recent loss.

"It's time to find somebody else," Johnson said in a video posting to his social media account.

Riley has a 42-21 record through his five seasons with USC. The Trojans have not reached double-digit victories since his first year with the team in 2022, when they finished with an 11-3 record.

articles.title: College Football Sunday Summary; Planes, Trains, and Automobiles
articles.summary: It was a crazy weekend, with ground stops affecting thousands of planes across the country and college football travel for teams and fans alike. College Foot...
articles.body:
It was a crazy weekend, with ground stops affecting thousands of planes across the country and college football travel for teams and fans alike. College Football Sunday Summary takes a look at who had a smooth flying experience, who had a weekend of turbulence, and where we are with planes, trains, and automobiles.

The most unhappy passengers from the weekend may be the Oklahoma Sooners. While the start times of some games got pushed back to accommodate adjusted travel plans, the Ole Miss game at Oklahoma got moved to an entirely different day, from Saturday to Sunday afternoon.

Apparently, even as the ground stop was lifted Friday night, Ole Miss could not get a charter flight due to plane and crew availability. So, the Rebels could not travel until Saturday. SEC Commissioner mandated that the game be changed to Sunday. Oklahoma was none too pleased. Apparently, Sankey was not in a mood for debate and threatened Oklahoma with a forfeit if they bucked him on the decision.

This got us to dueling press releases from the two schools. Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny issued a statement that said this was unfair to the fans who had their time commitments set for Saturday's game. And he added that it was unfair to the team because they focus their week of prep based on a specific schedule. "Put simply, this decision isn't fair to our athletes, our institution, or to Sooner Nation. But we've been given no other choice. We are obligated to play the game when directed, but we remain steadfast in our belief that the wrong outcome was reached this evening," he wrote.

Ole Miss athletic director Keith Carter wrote a memo explaining the flight/travel circumstances and how Ole Miss was the one team in the country that stayed grounded.

So no one is happy, and we will have college football on TV on a Sunday afternoon in a time/space where the NFL dominates.

USC lost at Indiana on Saturday night, 27-13. The Trojans are now 7-3 overall with all of those losses coming in Big 10 play, where they are tied for sixth place. They are out of the running for a college football playoff spot as they close out the season against Maryland and UCLA.

With the huge budget being spent on players and the coaching staff, there are no happy passengers on that flight. We would advise Lincoln Riley to stay away from airport tarmacs. We have seen USC do some ugly things to coaches there.

Lane Kiffin. Do we really need to say more? Ok, that was low-hanging fruit and was too easy to pick.

But Kiffin is getting his first-class seats taken away and given to someone else. No one else has more self-induced drama in their world than does Kiffin. His departure from every previous job was tumultuous, with leaving Ole Miss for LSU the most recent and ugliest.

But everyone in Baton Rouge was there to jump on the Lane Train, from the Louisiana governor to the season ticket holders and LSU students. And what did they get on the Lane Train? A bad aftertaste. After Saturday's loss to Texas and old colleague Steve Sarkisian, LSU is 6-4 overall and 3-4 in the SEC. No, SEC loyalists…you are not getting a four-loss team into the playoff. Your credentials are not all that. LSU just plays out the season now and then has half the roster sit out whatever bowl game it gets invited to.

Shane Beamer's entire season has been in turbulence at South Carolina. He was on the proclaimed hot seat even before the season started. Have a good first month, or you will be elsewhere by Halloween.

The Gamecocks started 2-3, and the in-flight emergency masks were about to come down for Beamer. But then South Carolina won four in a row, including a stunner over Tennessee. All of a sudden, Beamer was being offered extra bags of peanuts. And then came Saturday night and a loss to the worst team in the SEC, Arkansas, 34-6. Beamer was left to explain the loss and why star quarterback LaNorris Sellers did not play. He injured his ankle last weekend but was listed as probable on Friday's availability report.

Seller's replacement, Cutter Woods, threw three interceptions and had no touchdowns in his first full start. No peanuts for Beamer on the flight home from Fayetteville.

The Oregon Ducks hosted Michigan on Saturday, and don't be surprised if the Wolverines' luggage gets lost on the flight home. The Ducks abused the Michigan defense in the 31-7 win. Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola threw for 341 yards and four touchdowns. But here is the real exclamation point to those numbers. Three of the touchdown passes were for 49 yards or more.

And Oregon did so while wearing what they called their "Duckzilla" uniforms, which were all black. Who knew Ducks could be so mean?

The worst thing that happened to SMU over the weekend was that the Wake Forest team plane got into Dallas before the air traffic chaos on Friday. The Mustangs were a 1.5 favorite over the Demon Deacons . And then the game started. Final score: Wake Forest 49, SMU 7.

The poor SMU Shetland pony is now being used as an emotional support animal for the football team.

Wake Forest is now 9-1, has given up only 36 points total in its last six games, and is flying like a high-speed jet. Time for the playoff committee to track down the tail numbers and recognize the team.

Hey, speaking of Forest, or really Notre Dame, did you see that former Deacs and Irish quarterback Sam Hartman is on The Bachelor this season? His post-college football career has remained grounded, so the guy with the good hair who has done modeling for men's clothing companies is going to host a bunch of women who will try to woo him.

The folks at Last Word were the last ones to get in any questions with Hartman during his Wake Forest tenure. The question(s) after the Wake win in the 2022 Gasparilla Bowl were enough for him to walk off the stage and mumble something about getting drinks.

Knowing the details of his journey from Winston-Salem to the bowl game in Tampa to South Bend, we offer the following advice to the women of The Bachelor. Even if you think Hartman is yours, he could be dining with others; as long as someone else is batting their eyes at him, he is open to leaving. The transfer portal is never closed, ladies.

We end this column as we do each week with the Style Section. As Veterans Day was in the middle of the week this year, some schools did military appreciation days last week, and some did them this week.

We took special note of the helmets of the North Carolina Tar Heels and their tribute to military veterans. We are choosing not to dwell on the fact that the UNC team got into an on-field brawl at the end of the game with Louisville, and instead just applaud the effort to salute the veterans.

The Heels went with the retro UNC logo with the stars and stripes in the wordmark. They also included stars in the traditional argyle pattern across the top of the helmet.

articles.title: Alan Ruschel: Chapecoense plane crash survivor wins promotion in final match before retiring
articles.summary: Alan Ruschel, one of six survivors in the 2016 plane crash that was carrying members of the Chapecoense team, wins promotion to Brazil‘s Serie A in his final match before retiring.
articles.body:
Alan Ruschel, a survivor of the 2016 plane crash that was carrying the Chapecoense football team, won promotion to Brazil's Serie A in his final game before retirement.

Ruschel, 37, was one of just six survivors when the plane crashed in Colombia and killed 71 people, including 19 of the club's players and the coaching staff.

Despite severe injuries and spinal surgery, Ruschel returned to football a year later and retires after earning promotion to Brazil's top flight with Juventude, his boyhood club which he re-joined in 2023.

Ruschel came off the bench in the 74th minute to help see out a 2-0 win over Botafogo, resulting in an emotional farewell with a lap of honour at the club's Alfredo Jaconi Stadium.

Before the game, he was also carried into the stadium on the shoulders of fans.

"I arrived here in 2007 with the club in Serie A and I am leaving the club there as well," Ruschel told a Brazilian television station after the match.

"My body wasn't responding any more. I had two consecutive knee surgeries, so I was starting to fighting with my own body.

"It wasn't working any more, even though being on the pitch was always a pleasure."

Ruschel referenced the plane crash in a video on social media which he posted the day before the game to confirm his retirement.

"Football has given me wonderful moments, but life has put me in front of challenges that I never imagined. November 29, 2016, a day that changed my life forever.

"I lost friends, companions and people with whom I shared dreams and projects.

"And God gave me a second chance. I didn't know if I would be able to play football again, but I believed that if I was here, there was still a purpose for my life.

"And today, I have the privilege of being able to choose the moment to say goodbye."

There were contrasting fortunes for Ruschel's former club, however, with Juventude effectively replacing Chapecoense in Serie A following their relegation after just one season in the top flight.

The club will return to Serie B having won just four games out of 34 during the season.

articles.title: Steelers' offensive keys to victory in Week 10 vs. Bengals
articles.summary: Here's a look at several offensive keys to victory for the Pittsburgh Steelers ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have an important Week 10 matchup in front of them, as a win over the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football would give them a firm hold of the number one spot in the AFC North division. But in order for the Steelers to walk out of Cincinnati with their seventh win of the season, there are a few offensive keys the team should follow closely.

From feeding their best player on offense to exploiting the Bengals' Achilles' heel on defense, here's a look at three offensive keys to victory for Pittsburgh in Week 10.

Hit the Bengals where it hurts — feed Jaylen Warren

Cincinnati's defense is allowing a league-worst 5.0 yards per carry, which should have Warren and the rest of the Steelers' offense foaming at the mouth. Warren has been unstoppable in 2026 and could single-handedly hand the Bengals their third loss of the season on Sunday.

Exploit the Bengals third-and-short woes

Did someone order another league-worst statistic? The Bengals' defense has been terrible in third-and-short situations, allowing opposing offenses to convert 76% (ranked No. 32 out of 32) of these opportunities. Pittsburgh has the fifth-best conversion rate in third-and-short situations on offense and should try to catch Cincinnati in these moments as often as possible.

Pittsburgh's yards after catch once again rank as one of the highest in the league, with 139.9 YAC yards per game. The Bengals, you guessed it, are allowing the most YAC yards on defense, with 135.3 yards after the catch per contest. Whether it's dump-offs to Darnell Washington, short passes to Germie Bernard, or even hitting Warren on a checkdown and just letting him play football, the Steelers need to rely on YAC in this matchup.

articles.title: Former Gunner ruled out for months after knee surgery
articles.summary: Former Arsenal academy defender Ryan Alebiosu is expected to be out for three-to-four months after surgery on a knee injury.Photo by Gualter Fatia/Getty Imag...
articles.body:
Former Arsenal academy defender Ryan Alebiosu is expected to be out for three-to-four months after surgery on a knee injury.

Former Gunner Ryan Alebiosu is currently on the books for Blackburn Rovers , but he's going to be out of action for the foreseeable future with a knee injury.

The ex- Arsenal academy defender had to undergo surgery, and the good news is that the procedure was completed earlier this week. The bad news is that a lengthy period on the sidelines is now expected.

Prior to the surgery, Blackburn manager Tony Mowbray had told the media Alebiosu would be out for "three or four months, maybe a touch longer".

Photo by Charlotte Tattersall/Getty Images

"It's a tough break for the football team because he does bring us an amazing ability to cover ground and join the attack really fast," Mowbray added.

"He's going to have to be really disciplined and do the hard yards until he gets himself back in the new year. It's not good news for us or for him."

Alebiosu joined Arsenal at the age of eight, beginning a 13-year spell that only ended in 2023. He made the bench for a couple of senior Gunners fixtures, but never made it on for his first-team debut.

Even so, it was always clear the defender would play at a good level, and he found a new home with Championship Blackburn Rovers in 2025. He's gone on to make 55 appearances for the side.

Alebiosu's Rovers career will now be on hold as he recovers from his knee injury, and we wish him all the best with that process.

articles.title: Argentine midfield legend heaps praise on Barcelona midfielder – “One of the smartest footballers”
articles.summary: Frenkie de Jong has continued to dominate headlines ever since his return to full fitness at Barcelona.The midfielder has most recently made the news for pic...
articles.body:
Frenkie de Jong has continued to dominate headlines ever since his return to full fitness at Barcelona.

The midfielder has most recently made the news for picking up back discomfort during the Netherlands' game against Greece. He has returned to Barcelona and is set to undergo tests on Monday.

In the midst of all this, de Jong has received high praise from Argentine midfield legend Esteban Cambiasso.

De Jong's return has been a boon for Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

In a recent interaction, Cambiasso has heaped praise on the Barcelona midfielder, calling him one of the smartest footballers in Europe.

"I have a particular admiration for Frenkie de Jong. For me, he is one of the smartest footballers around today," he said (h/t Mundo Deportivo ).

One can hardly argue with the Dutchman, who has continued to thrive at Barcelona despite immense competition, with his leadership being ever so crucial for the team.

Cambiasso is particularly impressed by de Jong's versatility and ability to silence critics through his performances.

"He has also proven that when he faced criticism, whether while playing as a centre-back or when adapting to different position," he said.

"He is the kind of player whose impact you might not notice much when he is on the pitch, but when he is absent, you feel just how much you miss him," he added.

De Jong will go through tests tomorrow. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Frenkie de Jong, though, will care little about the compliment from Cambiasso and more about his fitness, having picked up what appears to be discomfort in his pubis .

As mentioned earlier, the midfielder is set to undergo tests tomorrow in Barcelona, which will decide the actual extent of his problem.

Having only returned from a long-term injury layoff, de Jong and Barcelona will hope there is nothing serious and that the player will be available for the upcoming game against Villarreal.

With Rodri also injured, it is imperative for Barcelona that de Jong remains fit and healthy, as the club brace themselves for an important phase of the campaign.

articles.title: Social media reacts to LSU's last second loss to Texas
articles.summary: LSU football fells to Texas in the final seconds on Saturday night. Here's how social media reacted to the loss.
articles.body:
LSU football fell in heartbreaking fashion to Texas on Saturday. The Longhorns scored a game-winning touchdown to seal a 22-21 win in Baton Rouge, knocking head coach Lane Kiffin and his team out of contention for the College Football Playoffs.

The Tigers led for nearly the entire game. They held a 14-10 lead at halftime and extended the advantage to eight points heading into the fourth quarter. The offense stalled repeatedly as the second half wound down, giving the Longhorns more opportunities to take the lead.

Sam Leavitt and Arch Manning each threw three interceptions. Two of Leavitt's interceptions came in the red zone, and the Tigers also missed a field goal, illustrating LSU's missed scoring opportunities in a tight game. The Tigers cashed in on two of Manning's picks, finding the end zone on both ensuing possessions.

With four losses, LSU must finish out its season without hope of playing meaningful postseason football.

How did social media react to Texas beating LSU?

Marcus Spears was impressed with Sark's playcalling on the final drive.

LSU football alums Ryan Clark and Marcus Spears were among several figures in sports media to offer their takes on the LSU and Texas game.

Leavitt took heat from some social media users after throwing three interceptions. The LSU offense has negative yardage through its four fourth quarter possessions and punted on every one.

Social media users offered up differing takes on how responsible Kiffin and the coaching staff are for the loss as well as what the future looks like. Some, like Skip Bayless, believe the future is bright for Kiffin in Baton Rouge.

articles.title: Bill Belichick Reacts to Fight Caught on Video After UNC's Loss to Louisville
articles.summary: UNC head coach Bill Belichick was forced to step in when some Tar Heels players got into it with Louisville's players following Saturday's 16-14 loss.
articles.body:
UNC head coach Bill Belichick was forced to step in when some Tar Heels players got into it with Louisville's players following Saturday's 16-14 loss.

After the game, Belichick made it clear that he wasn't pleased with his players' involvement in the brawl.

"You play the game between the whistles. That's not what we're here for," Belichick said, per Bryan Logan of ClutchPoints. "We got out there and got everybody out as quickly as possible."
